scenarios.title: Scenario Q
scenarios.text: Pinecrest Medical Group (650 employees, California) discovered on a Monday that an HR coordinator's laptop was stolen from her car the previous Friday. The laptop was not encrypted. It contained a spreadsheet with names, Social Security numbers, and dates of birth for all employees, and a separate file listing employees on medical leave and their diagnoses. The coordinator had downloaded the files to work from home, although the company's policy forbids storing personal data locally.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

scenarios.title: Scenario R
scenarios.text: Valley Fresh Produce operates a packing facility in Salinas, California, with 240 employees. In June, the facility's warehouse temperature inside reached 88°F, and two employees reported dizziness. In July, an employee's hand was caught in a conveyor, requiring amputation of a finger. A supervisor removed the guard from the conveyor weeks earlier to speed up cleaning. The operations manager wants to wait until a full internal investigation is complete before telling anyone outside the company.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

scenarios.title: Scenario S
scenarios.text: Redwood Precision Parts (180 employees, Riverside, California) had a severe storm that flooded its only production building, closing it for an estimated three weeks. Payroll runs on a cloud system, but key personnel records are only on paper in the flooded HR office. Employees are asking whether they will be paid, and a key customer wants to know when orders will ship. There is no written business continuity plan.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 2

scenarios.title: Scenario T
scenarios.text: Cascade Home Health (a California home-care agency with 900 caregivers and 60 office employees) uses paper timesheets and a separate spreadsheet for scheduling. Payroll errors average 45 per pay period, caregivers often wait up to two weeks for corrections, and 30% of turnover in the last year cited pay problems. Leaders are considering a mobile-first workforce management system with electronic visit verification (EVV), GPS clock-in, and self-service pay stubs. Caregivers range widely in age and technical comfort, and many speak Spanish or Tagalog as a primary language.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 2

scenarios.title: Scenario A
scenarios.text: Lakeshore Regional Credit Union (LRCU) has 620 employees at nine branches and a call center in Glendale, California. On Monday the CEO announced by all-staff email that the 140-person call center will move to a remote-first model in six months and that supervisors will become "team coaches." Managers received the email at the same moment as staff. A pulse survey two weeks later shows: 58% of call-center employees agree with "I don't understand why this change is happening"; 71% of supervisors say they "have no answers when my team asks me questions"; and voluntary resignations in the call center have doubled since the announcement.

scenarios.title: Scenario B
scenarios.text: Delta Ridge Software (non-union, 210 employees, Pasadena, California) has a handbook rule: "Employees may not discuss compensation with coworkers or post about company pay on social media." After the CFO announced a pay freeze, six software engineers posted about it in a public online group and circulated a petition asking the CEO to reconsider. The CEO asks HR to discipline the six for "disloyalty" and to have the petition removed.

scenarios.title: Scenario C
scenarios.text: Sierra Pacific Health Partners (SPHP) employs 1,400 people in California and Oregon. An HR pay equity analysis of 300 clinical data analysts in California, controlling for job level, tenure, location, and performance rating, found that women earn on average 4% less than men in the same jobs. The gap is concentrated in 12 roles filled in the last three years. Interviews with recruiters reveal that starting offers are commonly set by asking finalists what they currently earn and adding 8% to 10%.

scenarios.title: Scenario D
scenarios.text: Harborview Foods, a non-union food producer with 450 employees in California, plans to close its Fresno packaging plant (85 employees) and shift the work to a new facility in Reno, Nevada, about 280 miles away. Twenty Fresno employees would be offered transfers, and 65 would be laid off. Severance would be offered in exchange for signed releases. The COO wants to announce the closure next week and separate the 65 employees 45 days later. The Fresno workforce is 70% Hispanic, and the average age is 51. The CFO's model projects annual savings of $2.4 million and one-time closure and transfer costs of $3.1 million.

scenarios.title: Scenario I
scenarios.text: Ridgeview Tech (300 employees, California) employs Devon, a customer support lead rated "meets expectations" in each of the past three annual reviews. Devon returned from California Family Rights Act (CFRA) leave 10 weeks ago and filed an internal complaint about unpaid overtime six weeks ago. His new manager, who joined four months ago, says Devon's ticket-resolution times are the worst on the team and wants to place him on a 30-day performance improvement plan (PIP) and terminate him at the end if targets are missed. The manager has no written documentation of prior coaching, and other team members with similar metrics have not been placed on PIPs.

scenarios.title: Scenario J
scenarios.text: Pacific Coast Foods (California) has 380 hourly employees represented by Local 1122. The collective bargaining agreement expires in 90 days. Management's goals are a three-year term, 2.5% annual wage increases, and shifting more health premium cost to employees. The union's priorities are 5% annual raises, job security language, and no health-cost shift. Last quarter the company had 14 grievances, six about attendance-point discipline, and two are heading to arbitration.

scenarios.title: Scenario K
scenarios.text: Meridian Engineering (700 employees, California) found in its engagement survey that "I see a future for myself here" scored 38% favorable among engineers with three to six years' tenure. Voluntary turnover in this group is 22% (versus 10% company-wide), and exit interviews cite "the only way up is management." The company has one technical ladder that caps at Senior Engineer. Several strong senior engineers were promoted into management in the past two years, and half have since returned to technical roles or left.

scenarios.title: Scenario L
scenarios.text: Crestline Retail (2,000 employees, California) must close 12 stores and has decided to eliminate 180 positions within the next four months. It will offer two weeks of pay per year of service in exchange for a release of claims. Survey data from the last reduction two years ago showed that survivors' engagement dropped 15 points, and voluntary turnover among top performers doubled in the following six months. Crestline also wants to maintain a positive relationship with departing employees because many are also customers.

scenarios.title: Scenario M
scenarios.text: Golden State Home Services (California) employs 60 field technicians. Each technician is paid $26.00 per hour and works four 10-hour days (Monday to Thursday) each week. There is no alternative workweek schedule adopted by secret-ballot vote. The company also pays a nondiscretionary monthly safety bonus. The operations director says, "Nobody works more than 40 hours in a week, so we don't owe overtime."

scenarios.title: Scenario N
scenarios.text: Harbor & Hill Hotels (1,500 employees in California, Nevada, and Arizona) has an engagement score of 58% favorable on "I understand my total compensation," 45% on "My benefits meet my needs," and 71% on "I'm paid fairly." The workforce includes a large group of hourly workers under 30, about 25% of employees are age 50 or older, and many hourly employees do not enroll in the 401(k), even with a 4% match. The benefits budget is flat for next year.

scenarios.title: Scenario O
scenarios.text: BrightPath Education, a California nonprofit with 220 employees, pays its program coordinators an annual salary of $62,000 and classifies them as exempt administrative employees. The coordinators spend about 70% of their time on scheduling, data entry, and answering routine parent inquiries, with little independent judgment on significant matters. A new CFO asks whether the classification is correct and whether the coordinators could be paid as salaried non-exempt employees.

scenarios.title: Scenario P
scenarios.text: Vantage Capital Group (a public company with 900 employees) has a board compensation committee that is reviewing the CEO's pay package. Last year, the CEO received a base salary of $950,000, a cash bonus of $1.8 million, and restricted stock valued at $4.2 million. Shareholders approved the say-on-pay vote with only 58% support, down from 91% the prior year, and proxy advisors criticized the bonus because it was paid even though total shareholder return (TSR) was below the peer median. Median employee pay is $78,000.

scenarios.title: Scenario E
scenarios.text: Bayfront Medical Supply (800 employees, California) will open a Sacramento-area distribution center that needs 120 employees within nine months. A labor market analysis shows local unemployment at 5.4%, median pay for warehouse associates at $21.50 per hour, and three large employers recruiting heavily in the area. Bayfront plans to pay $19.50 per hour. Bayfront's brand is unknown locally. At its existing site, 60% of past hires came from employee referrals, but the Sacramento site has no current employees.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 1

scenarios.title: Scenario F
scenarios.text: Coastline Logistics (300 employees, California) made a written offer to Maria for a warehouse supervisor role, contingent on a background check and Form I-9 verification. Earlier, the online application asked, "Have you ever been convicted of a crime?" It also contained a background-check disclosure combined with a release of liability in the same paragraph. The third-party consumer reporting agency's report shows a 2019 misdemeanor theft conviction. Maria is scheduled to start on Monday, May 4. The hiring manager wants to withdraw the offer immediately.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 1

scenarios.title: Scenario G
scenarios.text: Northgate Industries (1,100 employees in Fresno and Modesto, California) will sell its plastics division, which has 220 employees, to a buyer within six months. The buyer says it will hire "most" of the division's employees after individual interviews and will not guarantee comparable pay. The 18-person corporate HR, payroll, and IT group that supported the division will lose about half its workload. Northgate must also cut costs in the remaining business by 8%.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 2

scenarios.title: Scenario H
scenarios.text: Summit Health Group (1,600 employees, California) acquired Cedar Clinic Network (400 employees in California and Arizona) three months ago. Cedar employees kept their own handbook, benefits, and pay structure. Cedar's annualized voluntary turnover is 24%, compared with 11% at Summit, and its engagement scores are 22 points lower. Replacing a departing Cedar employee is estimated to cost $18,000. Cedar staff report hearing about decisions from the grapevine, are unsure how their retention bonuses work, and are confused about which paid-time-off rules apply. Summit plans to move Cedar to the Summit handbook in 60 days.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 2

scenarios.title: Scenario A4-S1
scenarios.text: Sagebrush Retail is a California retailer with 300 employees. Dana, a nonexempt associate paid $20 per hour, works at a store where associates must clear a bag check before leaving the premises after clocking out. Store managers also sometimes send associates home early when customer traffic is low.

scenarios.title: Scenario A1-S2
scenarios.text: NovaTech, an 800-employee company with a centralized, hierarchical culture, acquires Brightpath, a 200-employee firm with a flat, autonomous culture, mainly to gain its product engineering team. Leadership wants to keep Brightpath's engineers. Day 1 is in 30 days.

scenarios.title: Scenario A2-S1
scenarios.text: Larkspur Health, a California employer with 220 employees, screens 12 customer-service openings with a timed situational judgment test. Of 90 white applicants, 63 passed; of 60 Hispanic applicants, 30 passed. The posting states a pay range of $18 to $55 per hour, though the employer expects to pay $18 to $24, and recruiters ask candidates about their current pay.

scenarios.title: Scenario A3-S1
scenarios.text: Northwind Logistics, a California employer with 85 employees, places Priya, a dispatcher with three years of 'meets expectations' ratings, on a 60-day performance improvement plan for missed deadlines. Two weeks later she submits a physician's certification and requests 12 weeks of continuous leave for a serious health condition. Several of the missed deadlines fell on days she had told her supervisor she had medical appointments.

scenarios.title: Scenario A1-S1
scenarios.text: Meridian Foods, headquartered in Ohio with 400 employees, acquires a California distribution center with 80 employees at a single establishment. The center also uses 30 delivery drivers engaged as independent contractors. They are paid per route, drive company-branded trucks, and follow dispatcher schedules. Meridian plans to close the center in eight months and consolidate operations in Nevada.

scenarios.title: Scenario A3-S2
scenarios.text: Harbor Foods, a nonunion California food processor with 150 employees at a single plant, faces a union organizing campaign. Assume the union wins the election and is certified, then bargaining begins and, later, the union calls a strike over wages.

questions.stem: An HR generalist receives an urgent email that appears to come from the CEO, asking for all employees' W-2 forms to be sent to a personal email address today. The email address differs by one letter from the CEO's real address. This is most likely a ________ attack, and the correct response is to verify the request through a separate, known channel and report it to IT security.
questions.explanation: Targeted emails that impersonate executives to obtain sensitive data, such as W-2 information, are a well-known form of business email compromise. Verifying by phone or in person and reporting to IT prevents a data breach.
questions.otherNotes: "Ransomware" encrypts data and demands payment; it is not an email request for data. "Spam" is unsolicited bulk email and does not describe a targeted impersonation. Sending the data "because it came from the CEO" is the outcome the attacker wants.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Arrange the phases of selecting and implementing a new HRIS in order.

items.text: Configure, migrate data, and test
Define requirements and issue a request for proposal (RFP)
Train users, go live, and evaluate the results
Evaluate vendors and select the system
Conduct a needs analysis with stakeholders

questions.explanation: Requirements must come from documented needs, and vendors can be evaluated only against those requirements. Testing and training must happen before go-live, and evaluation confirms that the system meets its objectives.
questions.otherNotes: Selecting a vendor before defining requirements leads to choosing features rather than solving needs. Going live before testing risks payroll and data errors.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: A 300-employee California company plans monitoring software that records keystrokes, screenshots, and location on company laptops. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Install the software without notice, since employers may monitor anything on company-owned equipment
Abandon the plan, since electronic monitoring of employees is prohibited under California law
Define a purpose, limit collection, give CCPA notice, and restrict access and retention
Install the software and extend it to personal phones, so that monitoring is consistent across devices

questions.explanation: California's constitutional privacy right and the CCPA (as amended by the CPRA) require notice at collection, data minimization, and employee data rights; the NLRA limits surveillance of protected activity. A defined purpose, limits, notice, access controls, and communication also protect trust.

wrongReasons.A: This overstates employer rights; California privacy law and the CCPA require notice and limits.
wrongReasons.B: Monitoring is permitted in many circumstances with proper notice, purpose, and limits.
wrongReasons.D: Tracking personal devices and off-duty activity raises privacy and NLRA problems and goes beyond a legitimate purpose.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Under federal OSHA rules, an employer must report a work-related in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye to OSHA within ________ hours.
questions.explanation: Federal OSHA requires reporting of in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye within 24 hours (a work-related fatality has a shorter deadline). Cal/OSHA requires reporting of any serious injury, illness, or death immediately, but no longer than 8 hours after the employer knows or should have known.
questions.otherNotes: 8 hours is the federal deadline for fatalities and the Cal/OSHA deadline for serious injuries. 72 hours is not an OSHA reporting deadline.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Leaders want a generative AI chatbot on the HR self-service portal to answer benefits and policy questions. Which safeguard plan is best?

choices.text: Launch on the vendor's assurance of accuracy, since the vendor answers for any incorrect responses
Ban AI tools from HR entirely, since any automated answer could be inaccurate
Limit it to approved content, test it first, block storage of personal data, and route sensitive topics to staff
Launch with a disclaimer that answers may be wrong, and let employees decide what to trust

questions.explanation: AI can improve service, but HR stays accountable for accuracy and data protection. Approved content, testing and audits, privacy controls, escalation paths, governance with legal and IT, and routing harassment, accommodation, and leave topics to people manage the risks.

wrongReasons.A: HR remains responsible for the accuracy of information employees rely on, regardless of the vendor.
wrongReasons.B: Refusing any use ignores efficiency gains that safeguards can make safe.
wrongReasons.D: A disclaimer alone does not prevent harm from inaccurate guidance or protect personal data.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: A company had 6 OSHA-recordable injuries last year. Employees worked a total of 400,000 hours. Calculate the total case incidence rate (TCIR).
questions.explanation: TCIR = (number of recordable cases × 200,000) / total hours worked = (6 × 200,000) / 400,000 = 3.0. The 200,000 figure represents 100 full-time employees working 40 hours a week for 50 weeks.
questions.otherNotes: 0.000015 omits the 200,000 multiplier. 1.5 uses 100,000 as the multiplier.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: A California employer's outdoor landscaping crews work in temperatures that reach 97°F. Under Cal/OSHA's heat illness prevention standard, the employer must implement ________-heat procedures, which include observation for symptoms, pre-shift meetings, and mandatory cool-down rest periods for certain industries.
questions.explanation: Cal/OSHA's outdoor heat standard requires shade when temperatures exceed 80°F and high-heat procedures when temperatures reach 95°F or higher, in addition to water, training, and an emergency response plan.
questions.otherNotes: "Extreme" and "excessive" are not the regulatory terms. Shade is required at 80°F, but the 95°F threshold triggers the additional high-heat procedures.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: A company recorded 4 cases involving days away from work, restricted work, or job transfer (DART). Employees worked 320,000 hours. Calculate the DART rate.
questions.explanation: DART rate = (number of DART cases × 200,000) / total hours worked = (4 × 200,000) / 320,000 = 800,000 / 320,000 = 2.5.
questions.otherNotes: 1.25 uses 100,000 as the multiplier. 0.0000125 omits the 200,000 multiplier.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Which set of steps should HR take in the first 72 hours after learning of the stolen laptop?

choices.text: Wait to see whether the data are misused before deciding whether a response is needed
Terminate the coordinator for violating the data-storage policy and then close the matter
Notify every employee by email that their data are safe while the facts are reviewed
Activate the incident plan with IT and counsel, report the theft, and identify exposed data

questions.explanation: A fast, organized response limits harm and supports legal deadlines: involve IT security and counsel, report the theft, try to disable or wipe the device and change credentials, identify the data and affected people, notify the cyber insurer, and prepare notifications.

wrongReasons.A: Waiting risks missing notification obligations and lets harm spread.
wrongReasons.B: Discipline addresses one issue but not containment, assessment, or notification.
wrongReasons.C: Reassuring employees before facts are known is inaccurate and could undermine required notices.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Under California's data breach notification law (Civil Code section 1798.82), notice to affected California residents must be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay. If more than ________ California residents are notified of a single breach, a sample copy of the notice must also be submitted to the California Attorney General.
questions.explanation: California requires notification of affected residents when unencrypted personal information, such as a name combined with a Social Security number or medical information, is acquired by an unauthorized person. If more than 500 residents must be notified, the business must also send a sample notice to the Attorney General.
questions.otherNotes: 1,000 and 250 are not the California thresholds. The HIPAA threshold for notifying the media and HHS immediately is also 500, but it applies to protected health information held by covered entities.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Which set of changes best addresses the root causes of the Pinecrest incident?

choices.text: Encrypt devices, block local downloads of sensitive files, and keep medical data separate
Discipline the coordinator and remind all staff of the existing data-storage policy in writing
Ban remote work for all HR staff so that personal data never leave the office
Buy a cyber insurance policy that covers the cost of notifying employees after a breach

questions.explanation: The breach came from a behavior problem plus missing safeguards: no encryption, no technical enforcement of the policy, excess data in one file, and medical information stored with HR records. The ADA, FMLA, and California's CMIA require medical information to be kept separately and confidentially.

wrongReasons.B: This treats the breach as an individual failure and leaves the same technical gaps in place.
wrongReasons.C: Banning remote work is an overreaction and does not address encryption or access controls.
wrongReasons.D: Insurance transfers cost but does not prevent a recurrence.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: A California employee asks to see her personnel file and get a copy of her payroll records. What are the employer's deadlines?

choices.text: 21 calendar days for the personnel file and 30 calendar days for payroll records
No deadline for either, because personnel and payroll records are company property
Same day for both, because employees have a right to immediate access to their records
30 calendar days for the personnel file and 21 calendar days for payroll records

questions.explanation: Labor Code 1198.5 gives 30 calendar days to allow inspection or provide a copy of the personnel file after a written request, and Labor Code 226 gives 21 calendar days for payroll records. Penalties apply for noncompliance.

wrongReasons.A: This reverses the two deadlines.
wrongReasons.B: Employees have statutory inspection rights; records being company property does not defeat them.
wrongReasons.C: Statutory deadlines apply; immediate access is not required.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Employers must keep an employee's Form I-9 for three years after the date of hire or one year after the date employment ends, whichever is ________.
questions.explanation: The retention rule requires keeping Form I-9 until the later of the two dates. For example, an employee hired in 2020 who leaves in 2026 requires retention until 2027.
questions.otherNotes: "Earlier" would allow destruction too soon. "Longer than seven years" is not the federal rule.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Which statement about California's Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) is correct?

choices.text: Every employer needs a written program with inspections, investigations, and training
Only employers in hazardous industries need a written program for hazard inspections
Only employers with more than 10 employees need a written program for injury investigation
Every employer needs a written program, which covers only fire prevention and evacuation

questions.explanation: The IIPP is a written program, required of every California employer, to identify and correct hazards. Elements include a responsible person, compliance system, hazard communication without reprisal, inspections, investigations, timely correction, training, and recordkeeping.

wrongReasons.B: The IIPP is required of every California employer.
wrongReasons.C: Smaller employers have lighter recordkeeping rules but must still have a program.
wrongReasons.D: The IIPP covers hazard identification, correction, investigation, communication, training, and records, not just fire.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Most California employers must have a written ________ Violence Prevention Plan, which was required beginning July 1, 2024 under SB 553.
questions.explanation: SB 553 requires most California employers to establish, implement, and maintain a written workplace violence prevention plan, keep a violent incident log, provide training, and keep records. Exceptions include certain health care facilities covered by a separate standard and remote workers.
questions.otherNotes: "Active shooter" or "security" plans are narrower. The requirement is not limited to health care employers.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: An employee's doctor sends HR a note describing a diagnosis. HR also administers the company's self-insured health plan. How should HR handle the information?

choices.text: Treat the note as HIPAA-protected, since HIPAA covers all medical records an employer receives
Treat it as a confidential employment record kept apart from personnel and health plan files
Place the note in the personnel file, since the employee volunteered the information
Share the note with the health plan team, since HR administers that plan for the company

questions.explanation: HIPAA's privacy rule applies to the self-insured plan, which must be firewalled from employment decisions. The doctor's note is an employment record that the ADA, FMLA, and California's CMIA require to be kept confidential and separate. HR should request only what it needs, such as restrictions and duration.

wrongReasons.A: HIPAA covers the health plan, not employment records; this is a common misconception.
wrongReasons.C: The ADA, FMLA, and CMIA still require confidential, separate storage of volunteered medical information.
wrongReasons.D: Plan information must be firewalled from employment decisions, and employment medical records from the plan.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: OSHA Form 300A, the annual summary of work-related injuries and illnesses, must be posted in a visible location from February 1 to April ________.
questions.explanation: Covered employers must post the Form 300A summary from February 1 through April 30 each year, even if no injuries occurred. Records must be retained for five years.
questions.otherNotes: March 1 and March 31 are incorrect dates. The posting period is three months.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Which statement about employee self-service (ESS) in an HRIS is accurate?

choices.text: It lets managers approve team transactions, improving oversight but slowing processing
It lets HR staff enter all employee changes, improving accuracy but increasing workload
It lets employees update their own data, removing the security risks of HR data entry
Employees update their own data, which cuts HR workload but adds fraud risk

questions.explanation: ESS lets employees view and update information (address, withholding, direct deposit, benefits) and request time off online. It reduces HR workload and speeds processing, but needs security controls against fraud and support for employees without computer access.

wrongReasons.A: This describes manager self-service, a separate function.
wrongReasons.B: HR entering all changes is the opposite of self-service.
wrongReasons.C: ESS adds risks such as fraudulent direct-deposit changes; it does not remove security risk.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Under Cal/OSHA's indoor heat illness standard, an employer must take additional measures, including controls, when the indoor temperature or heat index reaches ________°F.
questions.explanation: Cal/OSHA's indoor heat illness prevention standard (Section 3396, effective July 2024) applies when indoor temperatures reach 82°F, requiring water, rest areas, and training. When temperature or heat index reaches 87°F (or 82°F for employees in clothing that restricts heat removal or in high-radiant-heat areas), the employer must evaluate and implement engineering and administrative controls.
questions.otherNotes: 82°F is the threshold for the standard's general provisions, not the controls requirement. 95°F is the outdoor high-heat threshold. 80°F is the outdoor shade threshold.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: How should HR respond to the operations manager's plan to delay external reporting of the amputation?

choices.text: Report it to Cal/OSHA now, since amputations must be reported within 8 hours
Report it to Cal/OSHA once the internal investigation is complete, so the facts are accurate
Skip the report if the employee returns to work, since lost time is what triggers reporting
Report it within 30 days on the Form 300 log, since the log is the required notice

questions.explanation: An amputation is a serious injury that must be reported to Cal/OSHA immediately, no later than 8 hours after the employer knows. HR should also log the case, investigate the removed guard, enforce lockout/tagout, report to the workers' compensation carrier, give a DWC-1 within one working day, and preserve evidence.

wrongReasons.B: Waiting for the investigation misses the 8-hour deadline; investigations run in parallel with reporting.
wrongReasons.C: An amputation is reportable regardless of whether the employee returns to work.
wrongReasons.D: The 300 log is a recordkeeping requirement; it does not replace the immediate serious-injury report.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: The procedure that ensures machines are properly shut off and cannot be started again before maintenance or cleaning is ________.
questions.explanation: Lockout/tagout procedures require isolating energy sources and applying locks and tags so machines cannot be energized while workers are exposed. Removing guards and cleaning without lockout is a major cause of amputations.
questions.otherNotes: "Machine guarding" protects during operation but does not address maintenance. "Hazard communication" addresses chemical hazards.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Match each data security term to its definition.

options.text: Limiting system access based on a user's job responsibilities
Collecting and keeping only the personal data needed for a specific purpose
Converting data into a coded form that only authorized parties can read
Requiring two or more forms of verification to log in
Malicious software that locks or encrypts data and demands payment

questions.explanation: Each term describes a distinct safeguard or threat. HR should understand them to work with IT on protecting employee data.
questions.otherNotes: Encryption and multi-factor authentication are often confused. Encryption protects the data itself; multi-factor authentication protects access to systems.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Under California's workers' compensation law, an employer must provide an employee with a DWC-1 claim form within one ________ day of learning of a work-related injury or illness.
questions.explanation: California Labor Code section 5401 requires the employer to provide a claim form within one working day of learning of the injury, and the employer must report the injury to its insurer.
questions.otherNotes: "Calendar" and "week" are not the statutory terms. Waiting for the employee to ask for a form is not permitted.

source.doc: HR Information Management, Safety, and Security Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Which set of elements must an OSHA emergency action plan include?

choices.text: Fire reporting procedures only, since other emergencies are covered under separate standards
Reporting procedures, evacuation routes, a post-evacuation headcount, and contacts
Evacuation routes only, since offices are not covered by the emergency action plan standard
Fire and evacuation procedures, written out by each employer regardless of its size

questions.explanation: Required elements include emergency reporting, evacuation procedures and route assignments, procedures for those who run critical operations, accounting for employees after evacuation, rescue and medical duties, and contacts for more information.

wrongReasons.A: The plan covers fire and other emergencies, not fire alone.
wrongReasons.C: A plan is required wherever an OSHA standard calls for one, including many office settings.
wrongReasons.D: Employers with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally.

questions.stem: A new employee self-service module will save 1,200 HR staff hours a year (at a loaded cost of $40 per hour) and $18,000 a year in printing and mailing. The module's annual subscription is $36,000. Calculate the net annual savings.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a business continuity plan from an emergency response plan?

Emergency response protects life and safety; continuity keeps critical operations running
Emergency response restores IT systems; continuity covers evacuation and first aid
Continuity covers only IT system backups; emergency response covers all other recovery

questions.stem: Which example best illustrates gamification in an HR context?

Employees take a personality assessment that sorts them into team-building groups
Employees earn badges and leaderboard points for completing required training modules
Employees receive a fixed annual bonus for perfect attendance during the year

questions.stem: An HR director learns that a machine operator whose job involves operating heavy equipment appears impaired at work, slurring his speech and stumbling, and he says he took his prescription pain medication. questions.stem: Arrange the steps of a workplace accident investigation in order.

items.text: Interview the injured employee and witnesses
Secure the scene and provide medical care
Identify root causes
Implement corrective actions and follow up
Collect evidence: photos, equipment condition, and documents

questions.stem: During a California facility closure caused by a natural disaster, non-exempt employees are generally paid only for hours worked (reporting time pay does not apply when work cannot begin or continue because of an act of God or other cause beyond the employer's control). questions.stem: Which plan best describes HR's role during the three-week closure?

choices.text: Wait until the building reopens, then explain pay and schedules to employees in person
Require all employees to use their accrued vacation to cover the closure period
Pay non-exempt employees reporting time pay for each scheduled shift missed during the closure
Communicate often on several channels, explain pay rules and unemployment, and find temporary work

wrongReasons.B: Forcing employees to use all vacation may not be permitted and damages trust.

questions.stem: After the storm, which HR records practice would most directly prevent the loss of personnel records in a future disaster?

choices.text: Store paper records in a waterproof, fire-rated filing cabinet in the HR office
Keep encrypted, access-controlled digital records with off-site or cloud backup
Keep a duplicate set of paper records at an HR manager's home
Scan records once a year and store the scans on a server in the same building

questions.explanation: Paper-only records in one location are a single point of failure. Digital records with off-site backup, access controls, encryption, and a retention schedule allow recovery and continued access.

wrongReasons.A: This reduces but does not remove the single point of failure.
wrongReasons.C: Home storage creates privacy and security risks.
wrongReasons.D: Backups in the same location share the same disaster risk.

questions.stem: Match each workplace hazard to the control that addresses it. (Each control is labeled with its level in the hierarchy of controls.)

prompts.text: A toxic solvent used in parts cleaning
Exposure to fumes during a short task
A slippery floor near a sink

options.text: Engineering control: an enclosure around the machine
Substitution with a less toxic solvent
Administrative control: warning signs and a cleaning schedule
Personal protective equipment: a respirator
Engineering control: a lift-assist device

questions.explanation: Each control fits one hazard. The hierarchy of controls, from most to least effective, is elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, and PPE, so in practice HR and safety staff should prefer the highest feasible level (for example, local exhaust ventilation would rank above respirators for fumes, and slip-resistant flooring above warning signs).
questions.otherNotes: Pairing the respirator with the solvent, or the warning signs with the noise, mismatches the control to the hazard: substitution removes the solvent hazard at its source, and signs do nothing to reduce noise exposure.

questions.stem: Why should HR keep personnel records, medical information, and Forms I-9 in separate files?

choices.text: Keeping them together in one locked personnel file meets the confidentiality requirements
Separation is optional and mainly makes files easier for supervisors to search
Different laws govern each, so separation limits access and keeps I-9 inspections narrow
Forms I-9 must be destroyed after hire, so only medical and personnel files need to be kept

questions.explanation: The ADA, FMLA, and California's CMIA require confidential, separate medical files. Separate I-9 files ensure only I-9s are produced in an inspection and keep immigration information out of employment decisions. Separation limits access, liability, and audit burden.

wrongReasons.A: Medical information must be separate from the personnel file, even if the file is locked.
wrongReasons.B: Separation is required for medical information and limits rather than expands access.
wrongReasons.D: Forms I-9 must be retained for three years after hire or one year after separation, whichever is later.

questions.stem: A company plans an internal social networking platform to improve collaboration. Which governance approach is best?

choices.text: A policy that bans discussion of pay or management decisions on the platform
No policy, so that employees feel free to use the platform in any way they choose
An acceptable-use policy that bars harassment and protects data but allows concerted activity
A policy that requires manager approval before any employee post appears on the platform

questions.stem: An employee injured on the job in California receives medical treatment and temporary disability payments through workers' compensation. Workers' compensation is generally the ________ remedy for workplace injuries, which means the employee usually cannot sue the employer in civil court for negligence.
questions.explanation: The exclusive remedy doctrine is the trade-off at the center of workers' compensation: employees receive benefits without proving fault, and employers are generally protected from tort suits. Exceptions exist, such as for certain intentional conduct.
questions.otherNotes: "Primary" or "preferred" remedy understates the rule. Workers' compensation does not bar claims for discrimination or retaliation.

questions.stem: Which plan would best help Cascade implement the new workforce system with its caregivers?

choices.text: Involve caregivers early, pilot first, train in several languages, and reimburse phone use
Roll out company-wide at once with English-only online training to speed adoption
Require caregivers to buy their own smartphones as a condition of using the system
Track caregivers' GPS location at all times, so that schedules can be adjusted quickly

questions.explanation: Implementations fail mostly on adoption. Early involvement, a multilingual vendor, a pilot, training in several languages and formats, device support or reimbursement, parallel processing, clear GPS policies, and outcome metrics address language, access, and trust.

wrongReasons.B: A single rollout with English-only training risks errors and resistance in this workforce.
wrongReasons.C: Requiring employees to buy devices without reimbursement may violate Labor Code 2802.
wrongReasons.D: Location tracking should be limited to working time with clear notice.

questions.stem: Leadership asks HR to justify the investment. Which measures best build and later evaluate the business case?

choices.text: Payroll error rate and cost, correction time, pay-related turnover cost, and ROI
The vendor's published claims about productivity gains at similar agencies
The percentage of caregivers who download and register on the app during the first month
The system's number of features compared with the current paper process

questions.explanation: A business case turns operational problems into financial terms with baselines and targets (errors, correction time, turnover cost, admin time, compliance risk, EVV compliance) and compares benefits with costs to calculate ROI and payback.

wrongReasons.B: Vendor claims are not evidence about Cascade's own problems.
wrongReasons.C: Adoption alone does not show whether payroll errors or turnover improved.
wrongReasons.D: Feature counts do not translate operational problems into financial terms.

questions.stem: Under California law, an employer that tracks employee location through GPS should limit tracking to ________ time and give employees notice of the tracking.
questions.explanation: California's constitutional privacy right, the CCPA's notice requirements, and Penal Code section 637.7 restrictions on tracking devices mean location monitoring should be tied to work purposes, limited to working time, and disclosed in advance.
questions.otherNotes: Tracking during "all" hours or "personal" time is not justified by business need and increases privacy risk.

questions.stem: A company's workers' compensation experience modification rate (EMR) rose from 0.92 to 1.25 over two years. Which response is best?

choices.text: Switch insurance carriers to reset the EMR and lower next year's premium
Discourage employees from reporting minor injuries so that fewer claims are filed
Accept the higher EMR, since it is average for companies in the same industry
Analyze claims by cause, fix leading hazards, and add return-to-work programs

questions.explanation: The EMR compares claims with the industry average (1.00). Moving from 0.92 to 1.25 raises premiums and can cost bids. Fixing injury causes, prompt reporting and care, modified-duty programs (consistent with ADA and FEHA), and claims management improve it.

wrongReasons.A: Changing carriers does not change the EMR, which follows the employer's claims history.
wrongReasons.B: Discouraging reporting is unlawful and increases the risk of serious claims later.
wrongReasons.C: An EMR of 1.25 is 25% worse than the industry average of 1.00.

questions.stem: A manager asks HR to send her the full spreadsheet of all employees' salaries, home addresses, and dates of birth so she can plan team birthday lunches. Applying the principle of least ________, HR should give her only each team member's birth month and day.
questions.explanation: The principle of least privilege gives users access only to the minimum data needed to perform a task. Birthday planning requires only month and day for team members, not salaries, addresses, or years of birth.
questions.otherNotes: "Access" and "disclosure" are general terms, not the principle. Sending the full data because the manager is authorized to see some of it ignores minimization.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an HR data retention schedule and why it matters?

choices.text: It requires keeping every HR record permanently, so nothing is lost if litigation arises
It allows destroying any record once HR no longer finds it useful for daily work
It lists which employees may access each HR record and from which devices
It sets how long each record is kept and how it is destroyed, subject to legal holds

questions.explanation: A retention schedule balances legal minimums with privacy and security duties not to keep data longer than needed. Consistent destruction is defensible, and legal holds must stop destruction when litigation is anticipated.

wrongReasons.A: Keeping everything indefinitely increases breach and litigation risk and cost.
wrongReasons.B: This ignores legal minimum retention periods and legal holds.
wrongReasons.C: Access rules are security controls, not a retention schedule.

questions.explanation: OSHA's exit route requirements and fire codes require that exit routes be unobstructed and that doors used for exits can be opened from the inside without keys, tools, or special knowledge.
questions.otherNotes: Requiring a badge to leave the building during an emergency violates exit requirements. Locking exits after hours while employees are inside is also a violation.

questions.stem: A manager reports that an employee threatened to "get even" with a coworker. How should HR respond under California's workplace violence prevention law?

choices.text: Treat the comment as a joke unless the employee repeats it or makes a specific threat
Assess risk, separate the employees, investigate, and log the incident under the plan
Terminate the employee immediately, since a threat justifies dismissal on its own
Ask the coworker to seek a restraining order, since employers cannot petition for one

questions.explanation: Threats are warning signs calling for prompt assessment, investigation, and action. Under SB 553, employers must record the incident in the violent incident log, follow the workplace violence prevention plan, and avoid retaliation against the reporter.

wrongReasons.A: Dismissing a threat without investigation ignores a potential risk.
wrongReasons.C: Terminating without investigation risks error and may escalate the situation.
wrongReasons.D: Employers (and, from 2025, collective bargaining representatives) may seek a workplace violence restraining order.

questions.stem: The CHRO has just received the board-approved business strategy: expand into two new states within 18 months. Arrange HR's actions in the most logical order.

items.text: Measure results against agreed KPIs and adjust the plan
Implement the initiatives and communicate them to stakeholders
Prioritize the gaps and design HR initiatives with budgets, owners, and timelines
Analyze the business strategy to define the workforce capabilities and headcount it will require
Compare current HR programs and workforce capabilities to those requirements to find gaps

questions.explanation: HR strategy is derived from business strategy, so the requirement has to be defined before anything can be compared to it. A gap analysis needs both the target state and the current state. Prioritizing and budgeting come only after the gaps are known, and measurement closes the loop and feeds the next planning cycle.
questions.otherNotes: Starting with benchmarking "best practices" or launching programs first is solution-first planning: it spends budget before anyone knows what the business needs. Measuring last does not mean measurement is optional; KPIs are agreed in step 3 so there is something to measure against.

questions.stem: A distribution company's largest warehouse sits in a wildfire-prone area. Analysis shows a moderate likelihood of a serious disruption, very high impact if one occurs, and relocation is not financially feasible. The CHRO recommends buying business-interruption and property insurance for the site. Using the four standard risk responses (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept), this recommendation is risk ________.
questions.explanation: The financial exposure is moved to a third party through insurance while the underlying hazard remains. That fits a risk that cannot be avoided and whose impact is too large to simply absorb.
questions.otherNotes: Avoid would mean leaving the location or dropping the activity, which the stem rules out. Mitigate means reducing likelihood or impact (defensible space, evacuation drills, a backup site); those are useful complements but they are not what insurance does. Accept is only appropriate when impact is tolerable, and here it is very high.

questions.stem: A company's strategic goal is to improve customer retention. In a balanced scorecard, which perspective-and-HR-measure pairing most directly links HR's work to that goal?

choices.text: Learning and growth: certification rate among customer-facing service staff
Learning and growth: total company headcount at the end of each quarter
Financial: benefits cost per employee across the whole workforce
Compliance: percentage of employees completing annual policy acknowledgments

questions.explanation: The balanced scorecard translates strategy into measures across the financial, customer, internal process, and learning and growth perspectives. Building service-staff capability is a learning-and-growth measure with a clear causal path to customer retention.

wrongReasons.B: Headcount has no causal path to customer retention, so it does not connect HR's work to the goal.
wrongReasons.C: Benefits cost per employee, by itself, has no logical link to whether customers stay.
wrongReasons.D: Compliance is not one of the four scorecard perspectives (financial, customer, internal process, learning and growth).

questions.stem: During the year the company had 66 separations. Headcount was 540 on January 1 and 460 on December 31. Calculate annual turnover rate using average headcount. Answer as a percentage to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Turnover rate = separations divided by average headcount, times 100. Average headcount = (540 + 460) / 2 = 500. 66 / 500 = 0.132, or 13.2%.
questions.otherNotes: 66/540 = 12.2% and 66/460 = 14.3% use only the beginning or ending headcount rather than the average. 66/1,000 = 6.6% forgets to divide the headcount sum by 2.

questions.stem: Overall annual turnover at a manufacturer stayed at 15%, but departures of employees rated "exceeds expectations" fell from 9% to 4%, and 80% of leavers are now employees rated "needs improvement." Overall turnover did not change, but the organization's ________ turnover improved.
questions.explanation: Functional turnover is departure of employees whose leaving does not hurt, or even helps, the organization. The mix of leavers has shifted from strong to weak performers, so the same headline rate now represents a better outcome.
questions.otherNotes: Dysfunctional (regrettable) turnover, the loss of valued employees, actually fell, so it is the opposite of the correct answer. "Involuntary" or "voluntary" describes who initiated the exit and cannot be determined from the stem.

questions.stem: In the ADKAR change model, the 58% survey result most directly signals a deficit in ________.
questions.explanation: ADKAR sequences Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement. Employees who say they do not understand why the change is happening have not yet reached the first stage, awareness of the reason for change. Later stages cannot succeed until this one is addressed.
questions.otherNotes: Desire would be indicated by employees who understand the reason but do not want to take part; the survey does not show that. Knowledge and Ability concern how to work in the new model and the skill to do it, which is premature when the "why" is not understood. Reinforcement applies after change has been adopted.

questions.stem: Which stakeholder group's handling contributed most to the situation, and what should HR have done with that group before the announcement?

choices.text: Call-center employees; require them to complete change-resistance training before the move
The CEO; persuade the CEO to postpone the announcement until closer to the move date
Front-line supervisors; brief them first with the rationale, talking points, and an FAQ
Branch employees; send them more frequent email updates about the call-center change

questions.explanation: Supervisors are the primary channel through which employees make sense of a change. Learning of it at the same moment as staff left 71% with no answers, which amplified confusion and attrition. Briefing key influencers first is core stakeholder management.

wrongReasons.A: This blames employees for resisting and misdiagnoses the cause; the survey shows they were never given the reason.
wrongReasons.B: The problem was sequencing and preparation, not timing; a later announcement handled the same way would fail the same way.
wrongReasons.D: Branch staff are not the group in the survey data, and more email does not fix the supervisors' lack of answers.

questions.stem: Which 30-day action-and-metric pair would best help stabilize the change?

choices.text: Send weekly all-staff emails about the move; track the percentage of those emails that are opened
Hold leader-led town halls on the reason; track pulse agreement that staff understand why
Hold leader-led town halls on the business reason; track year-end engagement survey scores
Announce retention bonuses for all call-center staff; track the annual voluntary turnover rate

questions.explanation: The survey shows employees lack the "why." Leader-led town halls address that directly, and a repeat pulse question on understanding the reason is a measure that can move within 30 days.

wrongReasons.A: Email volume does not address the missing "why" or the supervisors' gap, and open rates do not show recovery.
wrongReasons.C: The action fits, but a year-end score cannot show recovery within 30 days.
wrongReasons.D: A blanket bonus ignores the cause (no understanding of the change), and an annual rate cannot show 30-day recovery.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes an organization's mission statement from its vision statement?

choices.text: The mission describes where it wants to be in ten years; the vision states its current purpose
The mission lists the values that guide behavior; the vision explains how the work will be done
The mission sets measurable annual targets; the vision assigns accountability for meeting them
The mission states its present purpose; the vision describes the future state it aims to reach

questions.explanation: The mission explains what the organization does, for whom, and why it exists today. The vision is the aspirational future state. Strategy is built to move the organization from the mission toward the vision.

wrongReasons.A: This reverses the two: the mission is present-focused and the vision is future-focused.
wrongReasons.B: Guiding behaviors are values, and how work is done is strategy; neither defines mission or vision.
wrongReasons.C: Measurable targets and accountability belong to goals and performance management, not mission or vision.

questions.stem: Exit-survey data show turnover rising, and both pay and manager quality are frequently mentioned. To determine which factors predict who leaves while holding other variables constant, the HR analyst should run a ________ analysis.
questions.explanation: Regression estimates the independent effect of each variable on an outcome while controlling for the others, which is what is needed to separate the effect of pay from the effect of manager quality.
questions.otherNotes: Simple correlation shows association between two variables but cannot control for the others. A descriptive summary (averages, percentages) shows what happened but not what drives it. A trend line shows change over time but does not identify drivers.

questions.stem: Last year internal recruiting costs (recruiter salaries and tools) were $18,500 and external costs (advertising, agency fees, referral bonuses) were $61,500. The company made 40 hires. Calculate cost per hire.
questions.explanation: Cost per hire = (total internal recruiting costs + total external recruiting costs) / number of hires. ($18,500 + $61,500) / 40 = $80,000 / 40 = $2,000.
questions.otherNotes: $1,537.50 (61,500 / 40) omits internal costs. $462.50 (18,500 / 40) omits external costs. $200 comes from dividing $80,000 by 400 rather than 40.

questions.stem: A mentoring program is open only to employees of one race. Under Title VII, which redesign best removes the legal risk while still developing underrepresented talent?

choices.text: Keep the race restriction because the program's purpose of increasing diversity is a lawful goal
Open eligibility to all who meet neutral criteria, widen outreach, and track participation
End the company's mentoring, outreach, and pipeline programs to remove the legal exposure
Keep the race restriction but make participation voluntary and unpaid for those selected

questions.explanation: Title VII prohibits treating employees differently because of race, including access to development opportunities. Neutral eligibility, broad outreach, and monitoring pursue inclusion without conditioning access on protected status.

wrongReasons.A: A good purpose does not cure disparate treatment; excluding employees because of race is direct evidence of discrimination.
wrongReasons.C: This overstates the risk; open mentoring, outreach, and pipeline programs remain lawful.
wrongReasons.D: Access is still conditioned on race, so the program remains disparate treatment.

questions.stem: The federal law that prohibits employers with 20 or more employees from discriminating against workers aged 40 and older is the ________.
questions.explanation: The ADEA protects workers age 40 and over and applies to private employers with 20 or more employees. (California's FEHA also protects age 40 and over and applies to employers with 5 or more.)
questions.otherNotes: Title VII covers race, color, religion, sex, and national origin, not age. The ADA covers disability. The Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (OWBPA) amends the ADEA to govern waivers and benefits; it does not itself create the prohibition.

questions.stem: A leadership-development program cost $240,000 and produced measured benefits of $360,000. Calculate the program's ROI as a percentage.
questions.otherNotes: 150% divides benefits by cost, which is the benefit-cost ratio (1.5), not ROI. 33% divides the net benefit by benefits rather than by cost.

questions.stem: A company with sites in California, Texas, and Nevada wants one attendance and leave policy. Which approach best keeps the policy aligned while complying with state differences?

choices.text: Federal minimum standards adopted company-wide so that each site follows identical rules
A separate policy written by each site's manager to fit that state's legal requirements
One policy with managers granting state-law exceptions case by case when issues arise
One core policy with state addenda, one owner, manager training, and consistency audits

questions.explanation: Alignment means consistent principles and process across locations; compliance means meeting the applicable law in each place. A core policy plus state addenda achieves both, and owner, training, and audits keep it applied consistently.

wrongReasons.A: Federal minimums fall short of California requirements such as paid sick leave and CFRA.
wrongReasons.B: Site-written policies give up alignment and invite inconsistent-treatment claims.
wrongReasons.C: Ad hoc exceptions create inconsistent treatment and risk missing required state rights.

questions.stem: On a stakeholder power/interest grid, a stakeholder with high power and low interest in a proposed HR initiative should be kept ________.
questions.explanation: The standard grid strategies are: high power/high interest, manage closely; high power/low interest, keep satisfied; low power/high interest, keep informed; low power/low interest, monitor. Keeping a powerful but uninterested stakeholder satisfied prevents them from becoming an obstacle without over-investing effort.
questions.otherNotes: "Manage closely" is for stakeholders who are both powerful and highly interested. "Keep informed" applies to low-power, high-interest groups. "Monitor" applies to low-power, low-interest groups.

questions.stem: Which description of corporate social responsibility (CSR), with an HR example, is most accurate?

choices.text: Acting ethically and weighing stakeholder impact beyond legal minimums, such as volunteer time
Meeting legal requirements on schedule, such as filing EEO-1 reports by the federal deadline
Donating a share of profits to charity, such as an annual gift to a local food bank
Maximizing returns to shareholders, such as linking executive bonuses to the share price

questions.explanation: CSR is a commitment to operate ethically and consider impact on employees, communities, and the environment beyond what law requires. Paid volunteer time is an HR practice that puts it into action.

wrongReasons.B: CSR goes beyond legal minimums; compliance alone is not CSR.
wrongReasons.C: Charitable giving is one possible element, but CSR also covers workforce and operational practices.
wrongReasons.D: CSR extends accountability beyond shareholders to employees, communities, and the environment.

questions.stem: A business impact analysis sets a recovery time objective of 4 hours for payroll. A cold site takes about 72 hours to activate, a warm site about 24 hours, and a hot site (real-time data replication) under 4 hours. An outage is estimated to cost $95,000 per hour in penalties and lost productivity, and a hot site costs $180,000 per year. Payroll's recovery plan should use a ________ site.
questions.explanation: Only the hot site meets the 4-hour recovery objective. A four-hour outage would cost about $380,000, more than twice the annual cost of the hot site, so the cost is justified.
questions.otherNotes: A warm site (24 hours) and a cold site (72 hours) both exceed the 4-hour objective and would expose the company to about $2.28 million and $6.84 million in outage cost, respectively. Doing nothing (accepting the risk) has the same problem.

questions.stem: Match each strategic analysis tool to its primary purpose.

options.text: Scans political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental factors
Measures strategy through financial, customer, internal process, and learning and growth perspectives
Evaluates industry competitiveness, including rivalry, supplier and buyer power, and threats of entry and substitution
Assesses internal strengths and weaknesses and external opportunities and threats
Compares the current state with the desired future state

questions.explanation: Each tool answers a different question: SWOT looks at internal and external position; PESTLE at the macro environment; the balanced scorecard at performance measurement; Five Forces at industry structure; gap analysis at the distance between where the organization is and where it wants to be.
questions.otherNotes: The most common confusion is SWOT versus PESTLE. SWOT includes internal factors (strengths, weaknesses); PESTLE looks only at external, macro-level conditions.

questions.stem: A 12-employee California company asks which of Title VII, the ADEA, the ADA, and California's FEHA apply to it for discrimination claims. Which answer is correct?

choices.text: Only the FEHA, because it covers employers with 5 or more employees
Title VII and the ADA only, because both cover employers with 10 or more
All four laws, because each applies to employers with California employees
None of the four, because coverage starts at 15 employees under each law

questions.explanation: Federal thresholds are 15 employees (Title VII, ADA) and 20 (ADEA). The FEHA covers employers with 5 or more for discrimination (and all employers for harassment), so only the FEHA applies.

wrongReasons.B: Title VII and the ADA require 15 or more employees.
wrongReasons.C: The federal laws have size thresholds (15 for Title VII and the ADA, 20 for the ADEA) that this employer does not meet.
wrongReasons.D: The FEHA covers employers with 5 or more employees for discrimination claims.

questions.stem: Under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act, employees have the right to act together for mutual aid or protection. This kind of group action is called ________ activity.
questions.explanation: Section 7 protects non-supervisory employees, union or not, when they act together (or on behalf of others) to improve wages and working conditions. Discussing a pay freeze and circulating a petition about it is classic concerted activity.
questions.otherNotes: "Collective bargaining" refers to negotiation between an employer and a union, which is not occurring here. "Union organizing" is one type of protected activity but is narrower than the term the statute uses.

questions.stem: How should HR advise the CEO on the request to discipline the six engineers and remove the petition?

choices.text: Discipline the engineers for the social-media posts only, and let the petition stay in circulation
Proceed with discipline, because the NLRA protects only employees represented by a union
Advise against both: the activity is protected and concerted, and the rule is likely unlawful
Proceed with discipline, because the posts violate a handbook rule the engineers acknowledged

questions.explanation: Non-supervisory employees acting together about pay are engaged in protected concerted activity, so discipline risks an NLRA Section 8(a)(1) charge. The handbook rule should be revised, and HR should involve counsel and address the pay-freeze concerns.

wrongReasons.A: The posts are also protected concerted communication about pay, so discipline for them still risks an unfair labor practice.
wrongReasons.B: The NLRA protects non-supervisory employees in non-union workplaces too; this is a common misconception.
wrongReasons.D: A rule banning pay discussions is itself likely unlawful under the NLRA and California Labor Code 232, so it cannot justify discipline.

questions.stem: California Labor Code section ________ (numeral) prohibits an employer from requiring employees to refrain from disclosing the amount of their own wages.
questions.explanation: Labor Code section 232 protects an employee's right to disclose his or her own wages; section 232.5 protects disclosure of information about working conditions. Both apply in addition to the federal NLRA.
questions.otherNotes: Section 1102.5 is California's general whistleblower statute. Section 1197.5 is the California Equal Pay Act. Section 226 governs wage statements.

questions.stem: In Lewin's three-stage change model (unfreeze, change, ________), the final stage anchors new behaviors as the norm.
questions.explanation: Refreezing stabilizes the new state through reinforcement, policy, and culture so the organization does not revert to old habits.
questions.otherNotes: "Freeze" or "thaw" do not name the third stage; "unfreeze" is the first stage and is the opposite of the answer.

questions.stem: The CEO asks HR to justify a proposed 4% merit budget with external data. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Use a widely shared blog post on pay trends, because it reflects what employees are reading
Use the one survey with the highest projected increase, because it supports the proposal
Use several credible surveys, such as WorldatWork and BLS, treating planned budgets as actual pay
Use several credible surveys, such as WorldatWork and BLS, matched to jobs and aged

questions.explanation: Credible sources (WorldatWork salary budget survey, BLS Employment Cost Index, consultant surveys) must match the company's jobs, industry, size, and geography and be aged to the effective date.

wrongReasons.A: A blog post is not a credible or methodologically sound pay source.
wrongReasons.B: Picking the survey that supports a conclusion is biased, and one survey is unchecked for job match and date.
wrongReasons.C: Budget surveys show planned increases, not actual pay movement; treating them as actual misreads the data.

questions.stem: A California company with 140 employees will permanently close its only facility, ending all 140 jobs. The minimum advance written notice required under both the federal WARN Act and Cal-WARN is ________ calendar days.
questions.explanation: Both statutes require 60 days' notice. Federal WARN covers employers with 100 or more employees and a plant closing affecting 50 or more employees at a single site. Cal-WARN covers employers with 75 or more employees in the prior 12 months and a closing, relocation, or mass layoff at a covered establishment. Both are triggered here.
questions.otherNotes: 30 days is not the WARN standard, although it appears in other employment rules (for example, the 30-day window to request special enrollment in health coverage after a qualifying event). 90 days is not a statutory WARN requirement, although it may be a best practice for large reductions. Pay in lieu of notice does not eliminate the notice requirement; it is a remedy when notice is short.

questions.stem: A U.S. software company has 45 engineers, about 30% of its development capacity, in a country where political unrest is escalating. Which human capital risk strategy is best?

choices.text: Monitor news coverage of the unrest and decide on a response if conditions get much worse
Terminate the engineers' employment now to remove the company's exposure to the country
Assess scenarios with triggers, plan for duty of care, and shift some critical work elsewhere
Build a business continuity plan that moves all critical work to other sites within a month

questions.explanation: Treat it as a risk-management problem: assess likelihood and impact with trigger points, protect people through a duty-of-care plan, and reduce the 30% concentration through cross-training and redistributing critical work.

wrongReasons.A: Monitoring alone is passive; it sets no triggers and prepares no response.
wrongReasons.B: Immediate termination is a drastic avoidance response that ignores current likelihood and impact and creates legal and reputational risk.
wrongReasons.D: This addresses business capacity but omits duty of care for the employees and their families.

questions.stem: A culture audit finds that leaders say "safety first," yet the last three managers promoted had the highest output numbers and the worst injury rates. Employees say, "You get promoted for output." To make the stated value credible, HR's most direct lever is to change the ________ criteria.
questions.explanation: Employees read culture from what is actually rewarded. The values in use follow the promotion and reward system, not the posters. Changing those criteria to weigh safety outcomes aligns behavior with the stated value.
questions.otherNotes: More safety training or a new slogan leaves the incentive conflict in place. Firing the three managers punishes symptoms and does not change what the system rewards. Rewriting the mission statement changes the espoused value, which is not in question.

questions.stem: Managers are resisting a new performance-management process because they lack the skills to hold coaching conversations. Which strategy best fits the cause of the resistance?

choices.text: Facilitation and support, such as training and coaching for managers on the new process
Negotiation and agreement, such as offering trade-offs to managers who would lose something
Coercion, such as mandating use of the new process and tying compliance to bonus eligibility
Education and communication, such as emails that explain the business case for the change

questions.explanation: Kotter and Schlesinger's approaches to resistance depend on its cause. When resistance is driven by anxiety or skill gaps, facilitation and support (training, coaching) addresses the cause directly.

wrongReasons.B: Negotiation fits when a powerful group would lose something; the cause here is a skill gap.
wrongReasons.C: Coercion is a last resort when speed is essential; it increases resistance driven by skill gaps.
wrongReasons.D: Education fits resistance caused by missing information; these managers lack skills, not information.

questions.stem: The first step in Kotter's eight-step change model is to create a sense of ________.
questions.explanation: Kotter's steps begin with establishing urgency so that people see why change is necessary, followed by building a guiding coalition, forming a vision, and so on.
questions.otherNotes: "Vision" is the third step and "coalition" is the second. "Momentum" relates to generating short-term wins later in the model.

questions.stem: Which pairing of a primary financial statement with an HR-related item is correct?

choices.text: Income statement: pension and retiree-benefit obligations
Balance sheet: accrued payroll and PTO liability
Statement of cash flows: accrued paid-time-off liability
Payroll register: compensation and benefits expense

questions.explanation: The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities, and equity at a point in time, so accrued payroll and PTO liabilities appear there. The income statement shows expenses over a period, and the cash flow statement shows cash in and out.

wrongReasons.A: Benefit obligations are liabilities and appear on the balance sheet; the income statement shows the related expense.
wrongReasons.C: An accrued liability is a balance-sheet item; the cash flow statement shows cash actually paid.
wrongReasons.D: A payroll register is an internal record, not one of the three primary financial statements.

questions.stem: The HR department's budget was $500,000, and actual spending was $530,000. This is a $30,000 (6%) ________ variance.
questions.explanation: A variance is favorable when actual spending is below budget and unfavorable when it is above. Spending exceeded the budget by $30,000, or 6% of the budget.
questions.otherNotes: "Favorable" would apply if spending had come in under budget. "Neutral" or "flexible" are not standard variance labels.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes FMLA eligibility and one way California's CFRA differs?

choices.text: FMLA requires 6 months of service and 1,000 hours; CFRA requires 12 months and 1,250 hours
FMLA needs 12 months, 1,250 hours, and 50 employees in 75 miles; CFRA has no 75-mile test
FMLA covers employers with 15 or more employees; CFRA covers employers with 50 or more
FMLA requires 12 months, 1,250 hours, and 50 employees within 75 miles; CFRA adds the same test

questions.explanation: FMLA eligibility requires 12 months of employment, 1,250 hours in the prior 12 months, and a worksite with 50 or more employees within 75 miles. CFRA covers employers with 5 or more employees and has no 75-mile test.

wrongReasons.A: FMLA requires 12 months of employment and 1,250 hours; 6 months and 1,000 hours are not the FMLA tests.
wrongReasons.C: Fifteen is the Title VII and ADA threshold; FMLA covers 50 or more, and CFRA covers 5 or more.
wrongReasons.D: CFRA has no 75-mile worksite test; that is one of its key differences from the FMLA.

questions.stem: An HR leader is completing a first-ever human capital risk analysis. Arrange the steps in the most logical order.

items.text: Identify potential human capital risks, such as key-person dependence, skill shortages, and compliance exposure
Implement the responses and prepare contingency plans
Monitor the risks and report changes to leadership
Assess each risk's likelihood and potential impact
Prioritize the risks and select a response (avoid, mitigate, transfer, or accept)

questions.explanation: Risk cannot be assessed until it has been identified, and responses cannot be chosen until likelihood and impact are known. Monitoring closes the loop because risks change over time.
questions.otherNotes: Choosing responses before assessing risks leads to spending on low-priority exposures. Treating monitoring as optional leaves the plan stale.

questions.stem: California Labor Code section 432.3 prohibits employers from seeking or relying on an applicant's ________ history as a factor in deciding whether to make an offer or what pay to offer.
questions.explanation: California bars employers from asking about or relying on salary history. Recruiters may ask about salary expectations, and the employer must give an applicant the pay scale for the position on reasonable request. Anchoring offers to current pay carries prior pay disparities forward.
questions.otherNotes: "Employment" or "education" history are not restricted by this section. "Criminal" history is governed by a separate provision (the Fair Chance Act).

questions.stem: Which corrective action plan best addresses SPHP's pay-equity findings?
