choices.text: Make equity adjustments for the affected analysts and keep the current method of setting offers
End salary-history offers going forward and leave existing analysts' pay as it is
End salary-history offers, base offers on role ranges, and make privileged equity adjustments
Lower the pay of the higher-paid male analysts so that both groups earn the same amount

questions.explanation: The data show a symptom (an unexplained gap) and its cause (salary-history-based offers). An effective plan fixes the cause, corrects the effect under attorney-client privilege, and adds regular monitoring. Asking about salary history is also unlawful in California.

wrongReasons.A: Adjusting pay without stopping salary-history anchoring would reintroduce the gap with each new hire.
wrongReasons.B: Stopping the practice without adjusting current pay leaves the existing inequity and legal exposure.
wrongReasons.D: The Equal Pay Act prohibits reducing a higher-paid employee's wages to equalize pay.

questions.stem: Under the California Equal Pay Act, pay comparisons are made for substantially ________ work, not only for identical job titles.
questions.explanation: California's Equal Pay Act (Labor Code section 1197.5) prohibits paying employees less than others of a different sex, race, or ethnicity for substantially similar work, viewed as a composite of skill, effort, and responsibility performed under similar working conditions. That standard is broader than the federal Equal Pay Act's "equal work" standard.
questions.otherNotes: "Equal" or "identical" describes the narrower federal standard. "Comparable" is used in comparable worth theories, which the statute does not adopt.

questions.stem: HR wants to identify employees most likely to resign next quarter using tenure, engagement scores, and manager changes. Forecasting future outcomes from historical data in this way is ________ analytics.
questions.explanation: Descriptive analytics summarize what happened, diagnostic analytics explain why, predictive analytics estimate what is likely to happen, and prescriptive analytics recommend actions.
questions.otherNotes: Descriptive analytics only report existing turnover. Prescriptive analytics would go further to recommend interventions. Diagnostic analytics explain past causes rather than forecast.

questions.stem: Which description best captures HR acting as a strategic business partner?

choices.text: Carrying out whatever leaders ask, quickly and accurately, using strong customer-service skills
Enforcing policies consistently across the business, using strong knowledge of employment law
Processing HR transactions efficiently, using HR systems and well-documented procedures
Working with leaders to solve business problems, using business acumen and data analytics

questions.explanation: Strategic partnership shifts HR from transactional service to shaping organizational outcomes. That requires business acumen, data and analytics skills, consulting and influence, credibility, and change leadership.

wrongReasons.A: This describes an order-taker role, not a partner who shapes business outcomes.
wrongReasons.B: This describes a compliance-only role; compliance matters but is not strategic partnership.
wrongReasons.C: Efficient administration is a transactional role, not a strategic one.

questions.stem: The company earned $147,000,000 in revenue with an average of 1,200 full-time equivalent employees. Calculate revenue per FTE.
questions.explanation: Revenue per FTE = total revenue / average FTEs. $147,000,000 / 1,200 = $122,500.
questions.otherNotes: $12,250 is a decimal-place error. $176,400,000 results from multiplying rather than dividing.

questions.stem: A U.S. company's country manager in Mexico wants to hire the customs inspector's niece "to smooth clearance." The federal statute most directly implicated is the ________ Act.
questions.explanation: The FCPA prohibits giving anything of value, including jobs, to foreign officials to obtain or retain business or an improper advantage, and it requires accurate books and records. HR should escalate to legal and compliance.
questions.otherNotes: Sarbanes-Oxley concerns financial reporting and whistleblower protection for public companies. The Fair Labor Standards Act concerns wages and hours. The Immigration Reform and Control Act concerns work authorization.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains how equity differs from equality in a DEI program?

choices.text: Equality adjusts support to each person's needs; equity gives everyone identical resources
Equity guarantees equal outcomes for each group; equality guarantees equal opportunity
Equity measures demographic representation; equality measures whether employees feel included
Equality gives everyone the same resources; equity adjusts support so people have fair access

questions.explanation: Equality means the same resources for everyone. Equity means fair treatment, access, and opportunity, recognizing that people may need different support. Equity efforts must still comply with anti-discrimination law.

wrongReasons.A: This reverses the two definitions.
wrongReasons.B: Equity focuses on fair processes and access; it does not guarantee equal outcomes.
wrongReasons.C: Representation describes diversity and feeling included describes inclusion; neither defines equity or equality.

questions.stem: Last year, 300 employees each had 250 scheduled workdays, and the company recorded 540 days lost to unscheduled absence. Calculate the absenteeism rate as a percentage, to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Absenteeism rate = days lost / (average number of employees × number of scheduled workdays) × 100. 540 / (300 × 250) = 540 / 75,000 = 0.0072, or 0.72%.
questions.otherNotes: 1.8% results from dividing by 30,000 (300 employees × 100 days) rather than 75,000. 7.2% is a decimal-place error.

questions.stem: After training, 95% of managers pass a test on the new coaching process, but observers find that 40% cannot perform the steps in real conversations without help. Using ADKAR, the element that most needs attention is ________.
questions.explanation: Passing the test shows the managers have knowledge, the "K" in ADKAR. The gap is the ability to turn that knowledge into behavior, which calls for practice, coaching, and feedback.
questions.otherNotes: Awareness and desire are likely present, because the managers took the training and passed. Knowledge is demonstrated by the 95% pass rate. Reinforcement comes after the ability exists and is used, to sustain it.

questions.stem: Twelve sales representatives left last year. The company estimates replacement cost at 50% of annual salary, and the average salary is $84,000. Calculate the total estimated cost of this turnover.
questions.otherNotes: $42,000 is the cost of a single departure. $1,008,000 uses the full salary rather than 50%.

questions.stem: Which legal risk in the COO's plan is most clearly triggered by the facts, and how should HR address it?

choices.text: The company is too small for WARN, so HR should rely on the severance offer to cover any gap
Severance replaces the notice requirement, so HR should increase severance to cover 60 days
Forty-five days is short of the 60 days WARN and Cal-WARN require; extend and give notice
Cal-WARN applies only to relocations within California, so HR should give the federal notice only

questions.explanation: Federal WARN and Cal-WARN both require 60 days' written notice for this plant closing or relocation. HR should extend the timeline and notify employees, the state and local workforce agencies, and local officials. Other risks to address include adverse impact and OWBPA release requirements.

wrongReasons.A: With 450 employees and an 85-person closure, both federal WARN and Cal-WARN apply.
wrongReasons.B: Severance is not a substitute for statutory notice under WARN or Cal-WARN.
wrongReasons.D: Cal-WARN covers relocations of 100 miles or more, including out of state, so the move to Reno is covered.

questions.stem: Using the CFO's figures, what is the simple payback period, and which people-related factor should the CEO weigh before approving the closure?

choices.text: About 9 months; the loss of skilled workers and know-how from staff who will not relocate
About 15.5 months; loss of skilled workers and know-how from staff who will not relocate
About 15.5 months; the lower monthly lease and utility costs at the new Reno facility
About 9 months; the lower monthly lease and utility costs at the new Reno facility

questions.explanation: Simple payback = one-time cost / annual savings = $3.1 million / $2.4 million = 1.29 years, or about 15.5 months. People factors such as lost skills, morale, employer brand, and transfer acceptance can reduce or delay the savings.

wrongReasons.A: Nine months comes from dividing savings by cost (0.77 years), which inverts the ratio.
wrongReasons.C: Facility costs are financial factors, not people-related ones.
wrongReasons.D: This inverts the payback ratio and names a financial rather than a people-related factor.

questions.stem: Under the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (OWBPA), an employee age 40 or older who is offered severance in exchange for a release in a group termination program must be given at least ________ days to consider the agreement.
questions.explanation: For an exit incentive or group termination program, the OWBPA requires 45 days to consider the release, plus 7 days after signing to revoke it, and written disclosure of the job titles and ages of those selected and not selected. For an individual termination, the consideration period is 21 days.
questions.otherNotes: 21 days applies to individual (non-group) separations. 7 days is the revocation period, not the consideration period. 60 days is the WARN notice period.

questions.stem: A new CEO is shifting strategy from lowest price to premium customer service. Which change to HR strategy best supports the shift?

choices.text: Hire for service orientation, and measure and reward satisfaction and resolution quality
Keep calls-handled-per-hour targets and add a customer-service slogan to recruiting ads
Add customer-service training while keeping pay and performance measures as they are
Reduce staffing levels to lower costs and use the savings to fund a service-quality bonus

questions.explanation: HR strategy follows business strategy. Moving from cost leadership to differentiation changes the capabilities and behaviors needed, so selection, training, performance measures, and rewards must all reinforce service.

wrongReasons.B: Volume targets reward the old cost strategy, and a slogan alone sends conflicting signals.
wrongReasons.C: Training without aligning pay and performance measures leaves the old incentives in place.
wrongReasons.D: Cutting staff limits the time needed for quality service, working against the new strategy.

questions.stem: Match each federal law to its primary focus.

prompts.text: Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act
Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA)

options.text: Sets minimum wage, overtime, recordkeeping, and child labor standards
Protects reemployment rights of employees who leave for military service
Requires advance notice of plant closings and mass layoffs
Sets standards for private-sector retirement and welfare benefit plans
Protects the right to organize, bargain collectively, and engage in concerted activity

questions.explanation: Each statute has a distinct core function: labor relations, layoff notice, wage and hour standards, benefit plan governance, and military reemployment.
questions.otherNotes: Confusion most often occurs between ERISA (plan governance and fiduciary duties) and the FLSA (wages and hours), and between the NLRA (labor relations) and the WARN Act (layoff notice).

questions.stem: A training program cost $46,000 in total and was delivered to 230 employees. Calculate the cost per participant.
questions.explanation: Cost per participant = total program cost / number of participants = $46,000 / 230 = $200.
questions.otherNotes: $500 and $20 result from arithmetic or decimal errors. $10,580,000 comes from multiplying instead of dividing.

questions.stem: After a sales-skills course, participants rated it 4.8 out of 5 and averaged 92% on the post-test. Three months later, call recordings show reps still use their old sales approach, and revenue per rep is flat. In Kirkpatrick's model, the first level at which the program fell short is the ________ level.
questions.explanation: Level 1 (reaction) and Level 2 (learning) are strong, but Level 3 (behavior) shows nothing changed, which explains why Level 4 (results) did not improve. The likely cause is a lack of manager reinforcement, tools, or opportunity to apply the skills, not the course content.
questions.otherNotes: "Reaction" (Level 1) and "learning" (Level 2) are the two levels that succeeded. "Results" (Level 4) is flat, but it is a downstream effect of the Level 3 failure.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes performance appraisal from performance management?

choices.text: Appraisal and performance management are two names for the same annual review event
Performance management is the disciplinary process used when an employee's appraisal is poor
Appraisal is the ongoing coaching process; performance management is the annual rating form
Appraisal is a periodic evaluation; performance management is the ongoing system around it

questions.explanation: Performance appraisal is the periodic evaluation and documentation of performance. Performance management is the continuous system of goals, feedback, coaching, appraisal, development, and links to rewards.

wrongReasons.A: Treating them as the same reduces performance management to a once-a-year event.
wrongReasons.B: Performance management covers goals, feedback, coaching, and development, not only discipline.
wrongReasons.C: This reverses the two; appraisal is the periodic evaluation.

questions.stem: Calibration reveals that one manager rated 90% of his team "exceeds expectations," although the team's results are below the company average. He says he did not want to hurt morale. This rating error is ________ error.
questions.explanation: Leniency error is the tendency to rate everyone higher than performance warrants. The manager's explanation and the mismatch between ratings and results point to it. The corrective step is calibration, rater training, and tying ratings to evidence.
questions.otherNotes: Central tendency would cluster everyone in the middle. Halo means one strong trait colors all ratings; the manager's rating is uniform because of his motive, not one trait. Recency would emphasize recent events, which the stem does not suggest.

questions.stem: The CFO retires in eight months. Internal candidate A will be ready in about a year; candidate B is ready now but is exploring outside offers. The external CFO market is thin. Which plan is best?

choices.text: Promote B to CFO now and tell A that the next senior finance opening will be offered to A
Wait for A to become ready and leave the CFO role vacant for the months in between
Retain B with a stay agreement, speed A's readiness, and choose through a transparent process
Begin an external CFO search now so that the company is not dependent on the two internal candidates

questions.explanation: The key risk is losing B, the only ready-now candidate, which would force an external search in a thin market. A strong plan addresses retention, accelerates A's readiness, uses a transparent selection process, and broadens the finance bench.

wrongReasons.A: Promoting B without addressing A risks losing A and skips a fair selection process.
wrongReasons.B: Waiting ignores the eight-month timeline and B's flight risk.
wrongReasons.D: Going straight to an external search in a thin market ignores strong internal talent.

questions.stem: A top individual contributor is promoted to manager, struggles with leading people, and performs worse than before. This situation illustrates the ________ Principle.
questions.explanation: The Peter Principle holds that people tend to be promoted until they reach a level at which they are no longer effective. It shows why promotion decisions should assess leadership potential and provide development, or offer a technical career track.
questions.otherNotes: The Pareto Principle refers to the 80/20 rule. The Hawthorne effect concerns behavior change when people are observed. "Dilbert" is a comic, not a management principle.

questions.stem: Match each motivation theory to its central idea.

options.text: People compare their ratio of inputs to outcomes with that of others
Specific, challenging goals with feedback improve performance
Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction, and motivators create satisfaction
Needs are arranged from physiological through self-actualization, and lower needs must be met first
Motivation depends on expectancy, instrumentality, and valence

questions.explanation: Each theory explains motivation from a different angle: needs, job factors, expected reward, fairness, or goals.
questions.otherNotes: Herzberg and Maslow are often confused. Herzberg focuses on job factors and separates dissatisfiers from motivators; Maslow describes a hierarchy of personal needs.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes coaching from mentoring?

choices.text: Coaching is reserved for poor performers; mentoring is reserved for high-potential employees
Coaching is a long-term career relationship; mentoring is short-term skill improvement
Coaching is advocating for someone's promotion; mentoring is formal classroom training
Coaching builds specific skills over a set period; mentoring guides long-term career growth

questions.explanation: Coaching is short- to medium-term and focused on specific skills or performance. Mentoring is a longer-term relationship in which a more experienced person guides career development, often outside the reporting line.

wrongReasons.A: Coaching supports employees at all levels, not only poor performers.
wrongReasons.B: This reverses the two.
wrongReasons.C: Advocating for opportunities is sponsorship, and mentoring is a relationship, not classroom training.

questions.stem: An engagement survey shows overall favorable scores of 74%. By item: "I am paid fairly" 72%, "My manager supports me" 70%, and "I can see a path to advance here" 41%. Exit data show 65% of leavers with two to three years' tenure cite "no path forward." Pay is at market. The retention investment most likely to have the greatest effect is ________.
questions.explanation: The lowest survey item and the most frequent exit reason both point to career growth. Pay and manager scores are relatively healthy, so investing there would deliver less benefit.
questions.otherNotes: Increasing pay would target an item that is already at market. Manager training would address a relatively strong score. A general engagement event does not address the specific driver.

questions.stem: Under California Labor Code sections 98.6 and 1102.5, a termination within ________ days after an employee's protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of retaliation.
questions.explanation: Effective 2024, California law presumes retaliation when an adverse action follows protected activity (such as a wage complaint) within 90 days, unless the employer shows a legitimate independent reason. Devon's complaint was six weeks (42 days) ago, and CFRA leave protections add exposure.
questions.otherNotes: 30 and 60 are not the statutory windows. 180 days is used for other purposes (for example, some administrative filing periods) and is not the presumption period.

questions.stem: What is the most serious problem with the manager's plan to put Devon on a PIP and then terminate him?

choices.text: It uses a PIP, which is an inherently risky tool that HR should not allow managers to use
It sets a 30-day PIP, when California law requires PIPs to last at least 90 days
It follows his CFRA return and wage complaint, without documentation and unlike peers
It is unnecessary, because at-will employment allows termination without a stated reason

questions.explanation: The plan closely follows two protected activities, which creates retaliation risk and California's 90-day rebuttable presumption. It also lacks documented coaching, contradicts three "meets expectations" ratings, and treats Devon differently from peers with similar metrics.

wrongReasons.A: PIPs are legitimate when applied consistently and properly; the PIP itself is not the problem.
wrongReasons.B: California law does not set a minimum PIP length.
wrongReasons.D: At-will status does not permit retaliation, which is unlawful regardless of at-will employment.

questions.stem: What should HR do before any PIP or termination is issued to Devon?

choices.text: Let the PIP proceed and see whether Devon meets the targets before deciding on next steps
Terminate Devon now, before the 90-day presumption period after the protected activity begins
Pause, review facts and comparators with counsel, and have the wage complaint investigated
Transfer Devon to a different team so that the new manager no longer supervises him

questions.explanation: Multiple protected activities occurred in a short period. HR should slow down, verify performance data against peers and prior ratings, check how leave affects metrics, ensure the wage complaint is investigated independently, and act only on consistent, documented standards.

wrongReasons.A: Proceeding builds a record that appears retaliatory.
wrongReasons.B: Terminating early to avoid the presumption is not a lawful strategy and strengthens a retaliation claim.
wrongReasons.D: An unrequested transfer soon after protected activity can itself be an adverse action.

questions.stem: Managers in your company rate employees very differently. Which description of calibration, and how it reduces bias, is most accurate?

choices.text: HR fits each team's ratings to a bell curve so that every team has the same distribution
Managers justify proposed ratings with evidence against shared criteria; outliers are adjusted
Each manager finalizes ratings independently, and HR reviews them after they are released
Employees rate their own performance, and the manager's rating is averaged with theirs

questions.explanation: In calibration, managers present evidence for ratings against common definitions, the group identifies leniency, severity, and demographic inconsistencies, and ratings are adjusted and documented before they are final.

wrongReasons.A: Forced distribution is a separate method and is not the same as calibration.
wrongReasons.C: Independent finalization is what causes inconsistency; calibration happens before ratings are final.
wrongReasons.D: Self-ratings are an input to appraisal, not calibration across managers.

questions.stem: In the ADDIE instructional design model (analysis, design, development, implementation), the final phase is ________.
questions.explanation: ADDIE stands for Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. Evaluation assesses whether the training met its objectives.
questions.otherNotes: "Execution" and "delivery" are similar in meaning to implementation, which comes before the last phase.

questions.stem: Arrange the stages of the performance management cycle in the correct order.

items.text: Monitor and coach: provide ongoing feedback and support
Appraise: evaluate performance against expectations
Review and reset: revise goals for the next cycle
Plan: set expectations and goals
Reward and develop: link results to pay, recognition, and development plans

questions.explanation: The cycle starts with clear expectations, includes continuous feedback, and ends with evaluation and action that feed the next cycle.
questions.otherNotes: Placing appraisal before goal-setting has nothing to assess against. Ending the cycle at appraisal misses the step where results produce rewards and development.

questions.stem: Employees of color rate inclusion 25 points lower, are promoted at 60% of the rate of white employees with similar ratings, and leave at higher rates. Which response is best?

choices.text: Set aside a share of promotions for employees of color until promotion rates are equal
Hold a heritage celebration event and publish a statement of the company's inclusion values
Increase recruiting of employees of color so that representation rises at entry level
Audit promotions for bias, use structured criteria and diverse panels, and open access

questions.explanation: Equal performance ratings with unequal promotion rates suggest a process or bias problem. Auditing decisions, structuring promotion processes, and opening access to development on a neutral basis is both effective and lawful.

wrongReasons.A: Race-based preferences in individual promotion decisions create Title VII and FEHA exposure.
wrongReasons.B: Events and statements alone do not change promotion or retention outcomes.
wrongReasons.C: The data show an advancement and inclusion problem, not a hiring problem.

questions.stem: A 500-employee company will spend $120,000 on a retention program expected to reduce annual turnover from 18% to 14%. Each departure costs $30,000 to replace. Calculate the program's ROI as a percentage in the first year.
questions.otherNotes: 500% divides gross savings by cost ($600,000 / $120,000 = 5.0), which is the benefit-cost ratio, not ROI. 80% divides the net benefit by savings.

questions.stem: When every employee can trace how individual objectives connect to team and organizational goals, the employee has a clear line of ________.
questions.explanation: "Line of sight" is the connection between an employee's daily work and the organization's goals. Cascading goals from organizational to department to individual level creates it.
questions.otherNotes: "Command" refers to the chain of authority. "Reporting" refers to the supervisory relationship. Neither describes goal alignment.

questions.stem: Which element is most important to Pacific Coast Foods' strategy for the upcoming negotiations?

choices.text: Prepare a detailed wage proposal and leave non-wage topics for the next contract cycle
Cost the proposals, map interests for trades, and address the attendance-policy grievances
Open with a final offer on all issues to signal firmness and shorten the bargaining period
Wait until the agreement expires before beginning negotiations, to increase leverage

questions.explanation: Effective labor strategy links business goals to the economics and the relationship: costing proposals, identifying interests behind positions, and using grievance data (attendance discipline) to fix friction, plus a communication plan, contingency plan, and counsel's review.

wrongReasons.A: A wage-only plan ignores the union's job-security and health-cost priorities.
wrongReasons.C: Opening with a take-it-or-leave-it stance is inconsistent with the duty to bargain in good faith.
wrongReasons.D: Starting late leaves no time to prepare and raises the risk of a work stoppage.

questions.stem: In a unionized workplace, an employee who reasonably believes an investigatory interview may lead to discipline has the right to request union representation. These are called ________ rights.
questions.explanation: Weingarten rights arise from NLRB v. J. Weingarten, Inc. and allow a represented employee to request a union representative at an investigatory interview that the employee reasonably believes could result in discipline. The employer need not offer representation but must honor a request.
questions.otherNotes: "Miranda" rights apply to criminal custody. "Garrity" rights concern public-employee statements. "Loudermill" rights concern pre-termination hearings for public employees.

questions.stem: An employer's refusal to bargain collectively in good faith with the employees' representative is an unfair labor practice under Section 8(a)(________) of the NLRA.
questions.explanation: Section 8(a)(5) makes it an unfair labor practice for an employer to refuse to bargain collectively with the representative of its employees. Making unilateral changes to mandatory subjects of bargaining, such as wages or health premiums, during negotiations can violate it.
questions.otherNotes: Section 8(a)(1) prohibits interference with employees' Section 7 rights. Section 8(a)(2) prohibits employer domination of a union. Section 8(a)(3) prohibits discrimination to encourage or discourage union membership.

questions.stem: Which description of the purpose and use of exit interviews is most accurate?

choices.text: Persuade the departing employee to stay, then make a counteroffer when appropriate
Learn why employees leave, then analyze patterns across departures to improve retention
Document the departure for the personnel file, then keep the notes confidential and unused
Confirm final-pay details with the employee, then process COBRA and benefits paperwork

questions.explanation: Exit interviews reveal reasons for leaving. The data are most useful when aggregated by department, manager, or tenure to guide changes, and they can surface legal risks that must be investigated.

wrongReasons.A: Persuading an employee to stay is a stay conversation, a different tool.
wrongReasons.C: Collecting the data without analyzing it wastes the information.
wrongReasons.D: Final pay and benefits are offboarding tasks, not the purpose of the exit interview.

questions.stem: Under the California Family Rights Act, an employee returning from protected leave must generally be restored to the same or a ________ position.
questions.explanation: CFRA requires reinstatement to the same or a comparable position, meaning one with the same or similar duties, pay, benefits, location, and working conditions. The FMLA uses the term "equivalent."
questions.otherNotes: "Similar" or "lower" positions do not satisfy the requirement. Reinstatement to a lower-paid role would violate the law.

questions.stem: A California employee resigns with 84 hours of accrued, unused vacation. Her final regular rate of pay is $32.50 per hour. What amount of accrued vacation pay must be included in her final paycheck?
questions.explanation: In California, accrued vacation is earned wages and must be paid at the final rate at separation: 84 × $32.50 = $2,730.
questions.otherNotes: A "use-it-or-lose-it" policy that forfeits vacation is unlawful in California. Paying at a prior, lower rate is incorrect.

questions.stem: A company must eliminate 40 positions across three departments. Which set of steps is most complete?

choices.text: Set job-related criteria, test adverse impact, check WARN timing, and meet OWBPA rules
Let each manager choose whom to release, then give notice on the last day of employment
Select employees with the highest salaries, then offer severance in exchange for a release
Delay announcing the layoff to avoid resistance, then provide final pay within 30 days

questions.explanation: A layoff carries legal, financial, and people risks. Job-related criteria, adverse-impact review, WARN and Cal-WARN timing, OWBPA compliance (45 days to consider and 7 to revoke in a group program), final pay on the last day, and survivor planning each reduce one of them.

wrongReasons.B: Manager preference with no criteria invites discrimination claims, and late notice can violate WARN or Cal-WARN.
wrongReasons.C: Salary-based selection can disproportionately affect older workers, and releases must meet OWBPA rules.
wrongReasons.D: Delaying notice can violate WARN or Cal-WARN, and California requires final pay on the last day for involuntary terminations.

questions.stem: A grid that plots employees by current performance on one axis and future potential on the other, used in talent reviews and succession planning, is called the ________-box grid.
questions.explanation: The 9-box grid places employees in one of nine cells (low, moderate, or high performance by low, moderate, or high potential) to guide development and succession decisions.
questions.otherNotes: "Four-box" or "six-box" grids exist in some organizations but are not the standard tool. The Boston Consulting Group matrix is a portfolio tool for products, not people.

questions.stem: A California company wants to end hybrid work and require five days on-site. Engagement data rank flexibility as employees' top benefit, and exit interviews show competitors offer hybrid schedules. Which course of action is best?

choices.text: Test the case with team data and consider role-based on-site days, with individual accommodations
Implement the five-day mandate on schedule, since work location is a management decision
Keep the current hybrid policy unchanged, since any change would harm employee engagement
Implement the mandate and decline remote-work accommodation requests so the policy stays uniform

questions.explanation: Work-arrangement decisions should weigh business needs against talent risk with evidence. A role-based approach can meet collaboration needs while limiting turnover, and accommodation requests still go through the interactive process.

wrongReasons.B: Implementing without evaluating impact ignores the retention and engagement evidence.
wrongReasons.C: Refusing to consider change ignores legitimate business reasons for more on-site time.
wrongReasons.D: Accommodation obligations under the ADA and FEHA remain regardless of the policy.

questions.stem: An employee's performance score is weighted 60% on goals and 40% on competencies. She scored 4.0 on goals and 3.0 on competencies (on a 5-point scale). Calculate her overall weighted score.
questions.otherNotes: 3.5 is the unweighted average. 3.4 reverses the weights (0.40 × 4.0 + 0.60 × 3.0).

questions.stem: A performance evaluation that gathers input from a manager, peers, direct reports, and sometimes customers is called ________-degree feedback.
questions.explanation: 360-degree feedback collects input from all directions around an employee. It is most useful for development, and it requires care if used for pay or promotion decisions.
questions.otherNotes: "180-degree" feedback uses only the manager and self-review. "Upward" feedback is from direct reports only.

questions.stem: Which career-development strategy best addresses Meridian's data on mid-career engineers?

choices.text: Give the three-to-six-year engineers a market pay increase while keeping the current ladder
Promote more senior engineers into management roles to show that advancement is possible
A dual ladder with technical levels equal to management in pay and influence
Offer tuition reimbursement for MBA programs so engineers can prepare for management careers

questions.explanation: Engineers see management as the only path up, and failed promotions confirm that forcing technical experts into management loses talent. A dual career ladder removes the forced choice; development plans and outcome metrics support it.

wrongReasons.A: Raising pay alone does not solve the lack of a path above Senior Engineer.
wrongReasons.B: Promoting more engineers into management repeats the pattern that has already failed.
wrongReasons.D: This still channels growth only through management, the path the engineers do not want.

questions.stem: A career structure that provides parallel advancement for technical specialists and for managers is called a ________ career ladder.
questions.explanation: A dual career ladder allows technical experts to advance in pay, title, and influence without moving into people management.
questions.otherNotes: A "broadband" structure combines pay grades; it is not a career-path model. A "lattice" career model emphasizes lateral moves, which can complement but is not the same as a dual ladder.

questions.stem: Calculate the number of additional departures per year in the engineering group relative to the company-wide rate, if the three-to-six-year group has 150 engineers.
questions.explanation: The group's turnover of 22% versus 10% company-wide is a 12-point difference. 150 × 0.12 = 18.
questions.otherNotes: 33 is the total number of departures in the group (150 × 22%). 15 is what departures would be at the company-wide rate.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes training from development?

choices.text: Training and development are the same activity described with two different terms
Training builds skills for the current job; development prepares people for future roles
Training is for front-line staff; development is a program reserved for executives
Training prepares employees for future roles; development builds current-job skills

questions.explanation: Training builds specific knowledge and skills for the current job with immediate application. Development is broader and longer-term, using experiences such as stretch assignments, mentoring, and rotations.

wrongReasons.A: The two differ in scope and time horizon.
wrongReasons.C: Development applies at all levels, not only to executives.
wrongReasons.D: This reverses the two.

questions.stem: Match each training need to the most suitable delivery method.

prompts.text: Teaching a new safety procedure for operating heavy machinery
Updating 2,000 employees on a new policy
Building negotiation skills in account managers
Preparing a replacement for a retiring expert's specialized knowledge

options.text: Job shadowing and structured knowledge transfer
E-learning module with a knowledge check
On-the-job training with demonstration and supervised practice
Action learning project on a real business problem
Role-plays and simulations with feedback

questions.explanation: The method should match the learning objective: hands-on skills need practice; broad information needs scale; interpersonal skills need rehearsal; strategic capability needs real problems; tacit expertise needs time alongside the expert.
questions.otherNotes: A classroom lecture for heavy-machinery safety skips the hands-on practice needed to build the skill. An e-learning module alone for negotiation lacks practice and feedback.

questions.stem: An organization-wide training needs assessment is normally carried out at three levels: organizational analysis, task analysis, and ________ analysis.
questions.explanation: Organizational analysis determines where training is needed based on strategy and results; task analysis identifies what skills a job requires; person analysis determines which employees need training and what kind.
questions.otherNotes: "Cost analysis" is part of evaluation. "Market analysis" is a business tool, not a level of needs assessment.

questions.stem: A company aims to grow revenue 10% while reducing customer churn, but the sales incentive rewards only new-customer bookings. Which change best aligns the incentive with the goal?

choices.text: Add a retention or renewal component and customer-quality goals shared with customer success
Keep the bookings incentive and add a company-wide message about the importance of retention
Eliminate the sales incentive so that reps no longer chase poor-fit customers
Raise the bookings payout rate so that reps bring in enough new revenue to offset churn

questions.explanation: What gets rewarded gets done. Adding renewal and customer-quality measures, shared with customer success, makes incentives reflect both parts of the objective; finance should review cost.

wrongReasons.B: The incentive would still reward behavior that contributes to churn.
wrongReasons.C: Removing incentives entirely removes motivation for growth.
wrongReasons.D: This intensifies the misaligned incentive and may increase poor-fit sales.

questions.stem: Of 40 employees in a leadership program, 32 completed all modules. Calculate the completion rate.
questions.explanation: Completion rate = completers / enrollees × 100 = 32 / 40 = 80%.
questions.otherNotes: 20% is the non-completion rate. 125% results from inverting the fraction.

questions.stem: A manager rates an employee "outstanding" in every category, including teamwork, based on her excellent technical work, although her peers report conflicts with her. This rating error is the ________ effect.
questions.explanation: The halo effect occurs when one strong trait causes a rater to give high marks in unrelated areas. The fix is to rate each dimension on evidence specific to that dimension.
questions.otherNotes: The horn effect is the opposite, where one weakness lowers all ratings. Recency error overweights recent events. Leniency raises all employees' ratings, not all categories for one person because of a single trait.

questions.stem: Which sequence best describes a typical union grievance procedure?

choices.text: Supervisor and steward, then a filing with the NLRB, then a ruling by an administrative judge
A lawsuit in state court, then mediation, then a final decision by the union's leadership
Supervisor and steward, then higher management, then senior leaders, then binding arbitration
Binding arbitration first, then review by senior management, then the immediate supervisor

questions.explanation: Grievances usually begin with the supervisor and steward, move in writing to higher management and union officials, then to senior leaders, and end in binding arbitration. The collective bargaining agreement sets the steps and time limits.

wrongReasons.A: An NLRB filing is an unfair labor practice charge, a separate process from the contract grievance procedure.
wrongReasons.B: Grievances follow the contract procedure, not litigation.
wrongReasons.D: This reverses the order; arbitration is the final step.

questions.stem: In the Thomas-Kilmann conflict model, when a decision is too important to settle for less and both parties' needs must be fully met, the most effective conflict style is ________.
questions.explanation: Collaborating is high on both assertiveness and cooperativeness. It seeks solutions that fully satisfy both parties and is most appropriate for important issues where the relationship matters and time allows.
questions.otherNotes: Compromising splits the difference, so neither party's needs are fully met. Competing prioritizes one party's goals. Accommodating yields to the other party. Avoiding postpones the issue.

questions.stem: Under situational leadership, which style should a manager use with a highly motivated new employee who lacks experience?

choices.text: Directing: clear instructions and close feedback, moving to coaching as skills grow
Delegating: hand over full responsibility, since the employee's motivation is already high
Supporting: share decisions and encourage the employee, since skills matter less than morale
Uniform: use the same style used with the rest of the team, so treatment stays consistent

questions.explanation: Hersey and Blanchard's model matches style (directing, coaching, supporting, delegating) to the follower's competence and commitment. High commitment with low competence calls for directing.

wrongReasons.B: Delegating to an inexperienced employee sets the employee up to fail.
wrongReasons.C: Supporting fits high competence with variable commitment, not low competence.
wrongReasons.D: Using one style for everyone is the approach the model argues against.

questions.stem: Arrange the steps of a progressive discipline process in the usual order.

items.text: Written warning
Coaching or verbal counseling
Final written warning (with or without suspension)
Documented verbal warning
Termination

questions.explanation: Progressive discipline increases in seriousness to give the employee notice and a chance to improve. Serious misconduct can skip steps if the policy preserves discretion.
questions.otherNotes: Starting with a final warning for a minor issue skips opportunities to correct. Terminating before any documented warning weakens the employer's record, unless the misconduct was serious.

questions.stem: A manager's regular one-on-one conversations with valued employees to learn what keeps them in the organization and what might cause them to leave are called ________ interviews.
questions.explanation: Stay interviews are proactive retention tools. Unlike exit interviews, they gather information while there is still time to act.
questions.otherNotes: "Exit" interviews take place after an employee has decided to leave. "Engagement" surveys are broader and anonymous.

questions.stem: An expatriate returns to the United States after three years in Germany. Which repatriation element is most important to retaining the employee?

choices.text: A relocation package that covers moving costs and temporary housing for the first month
A return role decided after the employee arrives, based on openings available at that time
A defined return role identified six to twelve months ahead that uses the experience
A larger expatriate allowance in the final year to reward completion of the assignment

questions.explanation: Repatriates are at high risk of leaving within one to two years, often because they return to unclear roles. A planned return role, supported by a home-country sponsor, repatriation training, financial counseling, and debriefing, uses their experience and reduces turnover.

wrongReasons.A: Treating return as a simple relocation ignores the career and adjustment issues that drive turnover.
wrongReasons.B: Planning only after arrival leaves the employee without a clear role.
wrongReasons.D: Allowances do not address the unclear roles and undervalued experience that cause repatriate turnover.

questions.stem: Which offboarding strategy for the 180 departing employees is best?

choices.text: Notify by email to protect privacy, then hold final pay until each employee signs the release
Announce in one large group meeting, then provide COBRA notices and unemployment information
Notify in person, then require each employee to release all claims, including non-waivable ones
Check WARN by store, use OWBPA-compliant releases, notify in person, and pay on the last day

questions.explanation: A respectful, compliant process reduces legal exposure and protects the brand with a workforce that is also a customer base. Cal-WARN is measured per covered establishment of 75 or more employees, so each store's headcount matters.

wrongReasons.A: Email notice damages trust, and withholding final pay until a release is signed violates California law.
wrongReasons.B: A mass meeting without individual support damages trust and ignores WARN and release requirements.
wrongReasons.C: California law makes some claims non-waivable, and releases must also meet OWBPA for workers 40 and older.

questions.stem: Based on the last reduction, which plan best retains and re-engages survivors?

choices.text: Rely on survivors' gratitude for keeping their jobs and avoid raising the topic again
Send the layoff announcement and return to business as usual as quickly as possible
Give survivors a one-time bonus and redistribute departing employees' work evenly
Explain the reasons honestly, hold stay talks with top performers, and pulse engagement

questions.explanation: Survivor syndrome (anxiety, lower trust, higher workload) is predictable and appeared last time. Honest communication, targeted retention for key people, workload clarification, support resources, and pulse surveys at 30, 60, and 90 days address it.

wrongReasons.A: Assuming gratitude ignores the prior data showing engagement and top-performer losses.
wrongReasons.B: Offering no further communication repeats the prior outcome.
wrongReasons.C: A one-time payment and heavier workloads do not address the anxiety and trust issues behind survivor syndrome.

questions.stem: Under California's Silenced No More Act, a separation agreement that includes a non-disparagement or confidentiality clause must state that the employee is not prohibited from disclosing information about ________ acts in the workplace.
questions.explanation: Under Government Code section 12964.5, as amended by the Silenced No More Act (SB 331), such clauses must include language stating that the employee is not prohibited from discussing or disclosing information about unlawful acts in the workplace, such as harassment or discrimination or any other conduct the employee has reason to believe is unlawful.
questions.otherNotes: "Confidential" or "business" acts are not the protected category. The law does not prohibit protecting trade secrets or the amount of a settlement.

questions.stem: A union may petition the National Labor Relations Board for a secret-ballot representation election once at least ________ percent of the employees in the proposed bargaining unit have signed authorization cards.
questions.explanation: A petition requires a showing of interest from at least 30% of the unit. Winning the election then requires a majority of the votes cast. (NLRB rules on employer responses to card-majority recognition demands have changed in recent years, so confirm the current standard before the exam.)
questions.otherNotes: 50% (a majority) is what a union needs to win the election or to request voluntary recognition, not to petition. 25% and 40% are not NLRA thresholds.

questions.stem: A severance plan provides two weeks of pay per year of service. An employee with 9 years of service earns $1,450 per week. Calculate the severance.
questions.explanation: Weeks of severance = 2 × 9 = 18. Severance = 18 × $1,450 = $26,100.
questions.otherNotes: $13,050 uses one week per year. $2,900 uses two weeks total.

questions.stem: Leadership wants to know whether the succession plan is working. Which set of metrics best evaluates it?

choices.text: Number of names on the plan, number of planning meetings held, and number of forms completed
Ready-now bench strength, internal fill rate, and successors' performance after promotion
Overall company turnover, overall engagement score, and total training hours across the company
Average tenure of successors, number of successors per role, and age of current role holders

questions.explanation: A succession plan aims at continuity and leadership quality. Bench strength shows coverage, internal fill rate shows whether the pipeline is used, and successor success shows quality.

wrongReasons.A: These measure activity, not effectiveness.
wrongReasons.C: Company-wide measures do not relate specifically to the leadership pipeline.
wrongReasons.D: Tenure and counts say little about readiness or whether successors succeed.

questions.stem: An employee earns $68,000 per year. The midpoint of her salary range is $80,000. Her compa-ratio, expressed as a decimal to two places, is ________.
questions.explanation: Compa-ratio = salary / range midpoint = $68,000 / $80,000 = 0.85. A compa-ratio below 1.00 means the employee is paid below the midpoint, which may be appropriate for a newer employee or may signal a need for review.
questions.otherNotes: 1.18 inverts the fraction (midpoint divided by salary). 0.15 is the gap below midpoint, not the ratio.

questions.stem: Arrange the steps for building a market-based salary structure in the logical order.

items.text: Set pay grades and ranges (minimum, midpoint, maximum)
Slot non-benchmark jobs and place employees in ranges
Define the compensation philosophy and target market position
Match benchmark jobs to salary survey data
Conduct job analysis and document job descriptions

questions.explanation: The philosophy defines where the organization wants to pay relative to the market. Jobs must be defined before they can be matched to surveys, and ranges are set from the market data. Non-benchmark jobs are placed last using internal comparisons.
questions.otherNotes: Setting ranges before collecting market data produces ranges with no external basis. Placing employees in ranges before jobs are defined risks inconsistent treatment.

questions.stem: A fast-growing tech startup has limited cash, expects to go public within five years, and is struggling to hire senior engineers. Which total rewards philosophy fits best?

choices.text: Base pay well above market to win senior engineers, with equity offered only to executives
Base pay below market with no equity, relying on the startup's mission to attract engineers
Market-median base pay with vesting equity, solid core benefits, and growth opportunities
Base pay at market median with large annual cash bonuses tied to quarterly revenue growth

questions.explanation: A rewards philosophy should fit strategy, finances, and the talent market. Limited cash and an expected IPO make equity with vesting the natural lever, paired with competitive base pay, essential benefits, and non-cash elements engineers value.

wrongReasons.A: Leading the market on base salary is unaffordable with limited cash.
wrongReasons.B: A lagging philosophy with no equity leaves no way to compete for senior talent.
wrongReasons.D: Large cash bonuses strain limited cash and ignore the IPO, the company's main rewards lever.

questions.stem: Under California law, one technician's straight-time pay for the week is 40 hours × $26.00 = $1,040. How much additional overtime premium does the technician earn for one week at this schedule, not counting the bonus?
questions.displayAnswer: $104 in overtime premium (8 overtime hours at time-and-a-half; total weekly pay of $1,144)
questions.explanation: Without a valid alternative workweek schedule, California requires overtime at 1.5 times the regular rate for hours worked over 8 in a workday. Each 10-hour day has 2 overtime hours: 4 × 2 = 8 overtime hours per week. The overtime premium is 8 × $13.00 (half-time) = $104. Total pay: 32 hours × $26 + 8 hours × $39 = $832 + $312 = $1,144.
questions.otherNotes: $0 would apply under federal law only, because the FLSA does not require daily overtime. $312 is the total pay for the overtime hours (8 × $39), not the additional premium. The director's statement reflects the federal standard, not California law.

questions.stem: How should Golden State Home Services respond to the operations director's position on overtime?

choices.text: Keep the four-by-ten schedule as it is, because the technicians prefer working four days
Switch to five 8-hour days going forward and treat the past schedule as closed
Ask technicians to sign individual waivers of daily overtime and keep the four-day schedule
Pay daily overtime now, compute back pay with the bonus, and consider an alternative workweek vote

questions.explanation: California requires daily overtime after 8 hours unless a valid alternative workweek schedule has been adopted by secret ballot. The company should pay overtime going forward, remediate past pay (including the bonus in the regular rate), consult counsel on penalties, and train managers.

wrongReasons.A: Employee preference does not cure the violation; without a valid alternative workweek, hours over 8 in a day earn overtime.
wrongReasons.B: This fixes the future but leaves the back-pay liability unremedied.
wrongReasons.C: Individual waivers are not valid; an alternative workweek requires a two-thirds secret-ballot vote of affected employees.

questions.stem: Why must the nondiscretionary safety bonus be considered when calculating the technicians' overtime?

choices.text: A bonus promised in advance for meeting set criteria is part of the regular rate
Bonuses are never part of the regular rate, so the safety bonus does not affect overtime
The safety bonus replaces the overtime obligation for any month in which it is paid
Only bonuses paid in each weekly paycheck count, so a monthly bonus is excluded

questions.explanation: Under the FLSA and California law, nondiscretionary bonuses (promised in advance and tied to criteria such as safety) are part of the regular rate. Overtime must be recalculated to include them; only discretionary bonuses are excluded.

wrongReasons.B: This confuses discretionary bonuses, which are excluded, with nondiscretionary ones, which are included.
wrongReasons.C: A bonus does not replace overtime; it increases the rate at which overtime is owed.
wrongReasons.D: Bonuses earned over longer periods must be allocated back to the workweeks in which they were earned.

questions.stem: Under federal law (FLSA), a non-exempt employee paid $20.00 per hour worked 45 hours in a week and earned a $90 nondiscretionary productivity bonus for that week. Calculate total pay for the week.
questions.explanation: Regular rate = (45 × $20 + $90) / 45 = $990 / 45 = $22.00. Overtime premium = 5 hours × 0.5 × $22 = $55. Total pay = $900 + $90 + $55 = $1,045. (California calculates the regular rate on a flat-sum bonus differently, which is why the stem specifies federal law.)
questions.otherNotes: $1,040 pays overtime only at 0.5 × $20 without including the bonus. $1,155 pays five overtime hours at the full 1.5 × $22 on top of straight time for all 45 hours, which double-counts the straight-time portion of the overtime hours.

questions.stem: A pay grade has a minimum of $50,000 and a maximum of $75,000. Its range spread, calculated as (maximum − minimum) / minimum, is ________ percent.
questions.explanation: Range spread = ($75,000 − $50,000) / $50,000 = 0.50, or 50%. Wider spreads are typical for higher-level jobs where there is more variation in performance and experience.
questions.otherNotes: 33% divides the difference by the maximum. $25,000 is the dollar width, not the spread percentage.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes internal equity from external competitiveness in pay?

choices.text: Internal equity means paying everyone the same; external competitiveness means paying the highest rate
Internal equity compares pay to the market; external competitiveness ranks jobs inside the company
Internal equity compares pay across demographic groups; external competitiveness compares benefits costs
Internal equity compares job values inside the company; external competitiveness compares to market

questions.explanation: Internal equity is fairness among jobs inside the organization, set through job evaluation. External competitiveness is how pay compares with other employers' pay for similar jobs, set through market surveys.

wrongReasons.A: Internal equity reflects job value, not identical pay, and paying the highest rate is a lead strategy.
wrongReasons.B: This reverses the two.
wrongReasons.C: Group comparisons are pay equity analysis, and external competitiveness concerns pay for similar jobs elsewhere.

questions.stem: The federal law that allows employees and their dependents to continue group health coverage for a limited period after a qualifying event, such as job loss, at their own expense is ________.
questions.explanation: Federal COBRA applies to employers with 20 or more employees. California's Cal-COBRA covers employers with 2 to 19 employees and extends coverage for some who exhaust federal COBRA.
questions.otherNotes: HIPAA's portability provisions address pre-existing condition limits and special enrollment, not continuation of coverage. ERISA governs plans generally. The ACA governs coverage mandates.

questions.stem: An employee earns $45.50 per hour and is in a range with a midpoint of $50.00. The merit matrix provides a 4% increase for "exceeds" performers whose compa-ratio is below 0.95 and 3% for those between 0.95 and 1.05. She is rated "exceeds." Calculate her new hourly rate.
questions.explanation: Compa-ratio = $45.50 / $50.00 = 0.91, which is below 0.95. She receives 4%: $45.50 × 1.04 = $47.32.
questions.otherNotes: $46.87 applies the 3% increase for the wrong compa-ratio band. $52.00 applies 4% to the midpoint rather than her current rate.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly contrasts a defined benefit plan with a defined contribution plan?

choices.text: A defined benefit plan sets contributions with employee risk; a defined contribution plan promises a set benefit
Defined benefit sets the benefit and the employer bears risk; defined contribution sets the inputs
A defined contribution plan is funded only by the employer; a defined benefit plan is funded only by employees
Both plan types guarantee the same retirement income; they differ only in how each is taxed

questions.explanation: A defined benefit plan (such as a pension) promises a specific benefit, usually based on salary and service, and the employer bears investment risk. A defined contribution plan (such as a 401(k)) specifies contributions, and the employee bears investment risk.

wrongReasons.A: This reverses the two plan types.
wrongReasons.C: Defined contribution plans often include both employee and employer contributions.
wrongReasons.D: Only a defined benefit plan promises a specific benefit; defined contribution results depend on investments.

questions.stem: Match each job evaluation method to its description.

options.text: Jobs are placed into predefined grades using written class descriptions
Jobs are ordered from highest to lowest in overall value
Jobs are valued primarily by what the external market pays for them
Points are assigned for compensable factors, and total points determine value
Key jobs are compared factor by factor, and a monetary value is assigned to each factor

questions.explanation: Ranking and classification are whole-job, non-quantitative methods. Point factor and factor comparison are quantitative. Market pricing uses external data rather than internal analysis.
questions.otherNotes: Point factor and factor comparison are often confused. The difference is that factor comparison assigns money values directly to factors of benchmark jobs rather than using points.

questions.stem: An employee's salary is $92,000 in a range with a minimum of $80,000 and a maximum of $120,000. Her range penetration, calculated as (salary − minimum) / (maximum − minimum), is ________ percent.
questions.explanation: Range penetration = ($92,000 − $80,000) / ($120,000 − $80,000) = $12,000 / $40,000 = 0.30, or 30%. It shows how far into the range the salary sits.
questions.otherNotes: 77% divides salary by maximum. 115% divides salary by minimum. Both describe different ratios.

questions.stem: Several long-tenured employees are now paid less than new hires in the same job because market rates rose quickly. Which response is best?

choices.text: Lower new-hire offers so that they no longer exceed the pay of current employees
Update ranges to market and make targeted, possibly phased, adjustments
Leave pay as it is, because the long-tenured employees have not raised complaints
Give every employee the same across-the-board increase this year

questions.explanation: This is pay compression, a structural problem from market movement outpacing internal adjustments. A durable fix corrects current inequities, checks for pay-equity issues across protected groups, and builds a regular market-review process.

wrongReasons.A: Lowering offers would hurt recruiting in a rising market.
wrongReasons.C: Waiting for complaints risks losing experienced employees.
wrongReasons.D: A uniform raise does not close the compression gap and is costly.

questions.stem: An employee's health plan charges a deductible of $1,500 and an 80/20 coinsurance after the deductible. The employee incurs $6,500 in covered charges. The employee pays $________ in total (assume no out-of-pocket maximum is reached).
questions.explanation: The employee pays the $1,500 deductible and 20% of the remaining $5,000 ($1,000), for a total of $2,500. The plan pays $4,000.
questions.otherNotes: $1,300 applies 20% to the full amount without a deductible. $1,500 includes only the deductible. $5,000 is the balance after the deductible, not the employee's share.

questions.stem: Health premiums are rising 12% a year. The CFO proposes moving all employees to a high-deductible health plan with an HSA and no other option. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Model effects by group, offer the HDHP beside another plan or fund the HSA, and add cost controls
Approve the proposal as written, since an HDHP with an HSA lowers premiums and encourages consumerism
Reject any change to the plans, since benefit cuts harm engagement and retention
Approve the proposal and drop coverage for part-time employees to save more

questions.explanation: Decisions should balance cost, employee need, and rewards strategy using claims and demographic data. Offering a choice or funding the HSA, adding cost-containment programs, educating employees, and checking ACA affordability and minimum value addresses both cost and risk.

wrongReasons.B: Approving without analysis ignores higher out-of-pocket costs for lower-wage and chronically ill employees, and retention risk.
wrongReasons.C: Rejecting any change ignores the 12% cost trend.
wrongReasons.D: Dropping coverage adds equity and possible ACA compliance problems without addressing the plan design issue.

questions.stem: For 2026, the maximum elective deferral an employee under age 50 can make to a 401(k) plan is $________.
questions.explanation: The IRS limit for elective deferrals in 2026 is $24,500. Employees age 50 or older may make an additional catch-up contribution ($8,000 for 2026), and those age 60 to 63 have a higher catch-up limit under SECURE 2.0.
questions.otherNotes: $23,500 was the 2025 limit. $7,500 is the 2026 IRA contribution limit, not the 401(k) limit. Limits are indexed annually, so confirm the figure for the year of the exam.

questions.stem: Which statement about white-collar overtime exemptions is correct for 2026?

choices.text: The duties categories are executive, administrative, and professional; the federal minimum salary is $1,128 a week
The duties categories are executive, administrative, and professional; the federal minimum salary is $684 a week
An employee whose job title is manager is exempt if paid at least $684 a week
An employee paid a salary of any amount is exempt if the employer classifies the role that way

questions.explanation: Exemption requires salary basis, salary level, and duties tests. After a federal court vacated the 2024 increases, the Department of Labor enforces $684 a week ($35,568 a year). California employees must also earn at least $70,304 in 2026 and spend more than half their time on exempt duties.

wrongReasons.A: The 2024 increase to $1,128 a week was vacated; the enforced federal level is $684 a week.
wrongReasons.C: Job title does not determine exemption; the duties test must also be met.
wrongReasons.D: Salary basis alone does not create exemption; salary level and duties tests apply.

questions.stem: A company gives a $100 gift card to each employee who reaches a five-year service anniversary. For federal tax purposes, this gift card is treated as ________ income to the employee.
questions.explanation: Cash and cash equivalents, including gift cards, are always taxable wages regardless of amount. Only tangible personal property given as a qualifying length-of-service or safety achievement award (not cash or gift cards) can be excluded, up to limits.
questions.otherNotes: "De minimis" treatment does not apply to cash or cash equivalents. "Tax-exempt" is incorrect for gift cards.

questions.stem: Which pair of characteristics most improves an employee recognition program?

choices.text: Annual and formal, presenting awards at a single year-end company event
Exclusive and selective, reserving awards for the same consistently top performers
Monetary and uniform, giving the same cash amount for every recognized action
Timely and specific, naming the behavior and its impact soon after it occurs

questions.explanation: Recognition reinforces behavior when it is sincere, timely, specific, and tied to organizational values, and when it is equitable, includes peers and managers, and offers meaningful choices.

wrongReasons.A: Recognition given only once a year is not timely.
wrongReasons.B: Recognizing the same few people undermines perceived fairness.
wrongReasons.C: Uniform cash rewards lack choice and meaning, and recognition works best when it is specific.

questions.stem: Which total rewards communications strategy best addresses Harbor & Hill's survey results?

choices.text: Add a new benefit next year and announce it in a company-wide email campaign
Send a detailed benefits guide by email to all employees during open enrollment
Personalized rewards statements, multiple channels and languages, and life-stage messages
Post the benefits plan documents on the intranet and invite employees to read them

questions.explanation: Low understanding scores show employees do not see the value of what they receive. Personalized statements, multichannel and multilingual delivery, life-stage messaging, and manager training are low-cost levers when the budget is flat.

wrongReasons.A: A new benefit without addressing understanding repeats the problem, and the budget is flat.
wrongReasons.B: Email-only communication misses hourly employees without company email.
wrongReasons.D: Plan documents are hard to understand and do not show the total value of rewards.

questions.stem: Harbor & Hill wants to increase 401(k) participation among hourly employees without increasing the budget. The plan feature that enrolls employees by default unless they opt out is called ________ enrollment.
questions.explanation: Automatic enrollment uses default behavior to increase participation, particularly among younger and lower-paid employees. SECURE 2.0 generally requires new plans established after December 29, 2022 to include auto-enrollment beginning in 2025, with exceptions.
questions.otherNotes: "Open" enrollment is the annual period to make benefit elections. "Voluntary" enrollment is the default approach that has yielded low participation.

questions.stem: With a flat budget, which approach would most improve "My benefits meet my needs" for both young hourly employees and employees 50 and older?

choices.text: Reallocate spending by utilization and add employee-paid voluntary benefits
Cut the 401(k) match and use the savings to fund a new benefit for all employees
Add one new benefit for every employee, funded by raising employee premiums
Keep the current benefits and repeat the same open-enrollment materials as last year

questions.explanation: A diverse workforce has different needs, so flexibility and choice raise perceived value without raising cost: reallocating based on utilization, voluntary benefits, flexible credits, and catch-up contribution education for workers 50 and older.

wrongReasons.B: Cutting the match reduces retirement security and could harm retention, especially among older employees.
wrongReasons.C: A single benefit for everyone does not address diverse needs.
wrongReasons.D: This leaves the low score and the needs gap unaddressed.

questions.stem: A pay range has a midpoint of $60,000 and a range spread of 40%, calculated from the minimum. Calculate the range minimum. Round to the nearest dollar.
questions.explanation: Minimum = midpoint / (1 + spread / 2) = $60,000 / 1.20 = $50,000. Maximum = minimum × 1.40 = $70,000. The midpoint is halfway between $50,000 and $70,000.
questions.otherNotes: $36,000 subtracts 40% of the midpoint. $48,000 subtracts 20% of the midpoint ($60,000 × 0.80), which does not produce a midpoint exactly between the minimum and a maximum that is 40% higher than the minimum.

questions.stem: A company wants to reward teamwork across a plant and share the savings from productivity improvements with all employees, using a formula based on the ratio of labor costs to production value. The incentive plan that best fits is a ________ plan.
questions.explanation: Gainsharing plans pay employees a share of measured productivity or cost savings, usually calculated at the plant or unit level. Scanlon plans use the ratio of labor costs to sales value; Rucker plans use value added.
questions.otherNotes: Profit sharing pays from company profits, which depend on factors outside the plant's control. Piece-rate plans reward individual output. Stock options reward share-price growth over years.

questions.stem: Arrange the steps of conducting a salary survey analysis in order.

items.text: Match jobs to survey descriptions based on content, not titles
Age the data to a common effective date
Choose relevant, credible salary surveys
Analyze the data and set the market rate for each job
Select benchmark jobs to price

questions.explanation: You must know which jobs to price before selecting surveys. Job matching must precede aging, and aging must be done before comparing data from surveys with different effective dates.
questions.otherNotes: Matching by job title rather than content produces poor matches. Analyzing data before aging it mixes data from different dates.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the ACA employer shared responsibility requirement?

choices.text: Employers with 50+ full-time employees, including equivalents, must offer affordable, minimum-value coverage to 95% of full-time staff
Employers with 50+ employees working 40 hours a week must offer affordable coverage to all full-time staff
Employers of any size must offer affordable, minimum-value coverage to all full-time staff or pay a penalty
Employers averaging 100 or more full-time employees must offer coverage to at least 70% of full-time staff

questions.explanation: An applicable large employer averaged 50 or more full-time employees (30+ hours a week), including equivalents, in the prior year. It must offer affordable, minimum-value coverage to at least 95% of full-time employees and dependents or risk a penalty, and must file Forms 1094-C and 1095-C.

wrongReasons.B: Under the ACA, full-time means an average of 30 hours a week (130 a month), and the offer threshold is 95%.
wrongReasons.C: The federal mandate applies only to applicable large employers with 50 or more full-time employees, including equivalents.
wrongReasons.D: The ALE threshold is 50, and the current offer standard is 95%; 70% applied only in a 2015 transition year.

questions.stem: California's paid family leave program, which provides partial wage replacement to employees who take time off to bond with a new child or care for a seriously ill family member, is funded through ________ contributions by employees.
questions.explanation: California Paid Family Leave is part of the SDI program and is funded by employee payroll deductions. It provides wage replacement but does not itself provide job protection; job protection comes from CFRA, the FMLA, or other laws.
questions.otherNotes: It is not funded by employer contributions or by the unemployment insurance fund. It is not the same as CFRA, which provides job protection but not pay.

questions.stem: Under California law in 2026, the minimum annual salary for the administrative exemption is $________.
questions.explanation: California requires exempt employees to earn at least twice the state minimum wage for full-time work. With the 2026 state minimum wage of $16.90: $16.90 × 2 × 2,080 = $70,304. The coordinators' salary of $62,000 is below this threshold, so they cannot be exempt in California regardless of their duties.
questions.otherNotes: $35,568 is the federal threshold currently enforced. $68,640 was the 2025 California threshold. Local minimum wage ordinances do not change the state exempt threshold, which is tied to the state minimum wage.

questions.stem: Apart from salary, why do the coordinators likely fail California's duties test for the administrative exemption?

choices.text: Their job title, coordinator, is not one of the titles that California treats as exempt
They spend about 70% of their time on routine clerical work rather than exempt duties
Their nonprofit employer is not eligible to classify any employees as exempt under state law
Their work involves parents rather than business clients, so the exemption cannot apply

questions.explanation: California requires exempt employees to be primarily engaged (more than 50% of work time) in exempt duties. Scheduling, data entry, and routine inquiries involve little discretion and independent judgment on matters of significance, a stricter test than the federal primary-duty standard.

wrongReasons.A: Job title does not determine exempt status; duties do.
wrongReasons.C: Nonprofit employers can classify employees as exempt when the tests are met.
wrongReasons.D: The exemption turns on the nature of the duties and judgment exercised, not who is served.

questions.stem: How should BrightPath correct the coordinators' classification?

choices.text: Reclassify as non-exempt, pay daily and weekly overtime, and calculate back wages
Raise their salaries to $70,304 and keep them classified as exempt administrative employees
Keep the current classification because none of the coordinators has filed a complaint
Reclassify them as non-exempt hourly employees and treat the past period as fully resolved

questions.explanation: The classification fails both salary and duties. As non-exempt employees, the coordinators may stay salaried but must receive overtime, meal and rest periods, time records, and itemized statements. Remediating past wages with counsel reduces wage-claim and PAGA exposure.

wrongReasons.B: Raising salary does not fix the failed duties test.
wrongReasons.C: Taking no action leaves the wage liability growing.
wrongReasons.D: Reclassifying without remediating past unpaid overtime and missed breaks leaves back-pay exposure.

questions.stem: An employer offers a 401(k) match of 100% on the first 3% of pay and 50% on the next 2%. An employee earning $80,000 contributes 5% of pay. Calculate the employer's matching contribution.
questions.explanation: 100% match on 3% = $2,400. 50% match on the next 2% = 0.5 × $1,600 = $800. Total match = $3,200 (4% of pay).
questions.otherNotes: $4,000 matches the full 5% at 100%. $2,400 includes only the first tier.

citations: Los Angeles Mun. Code ch. XVIII, art. 7
questions.stem: A non-exempt employee works in the City of Los Angeles and is paid the California minimum wage. Which minimum wage applies?

choices.text: The city's rate, because the highest rate that applies where the work is done governs
The state minimum wage, because the employer is headquartered in another California city
The federal minimum wage, because federal law takes precedence over state and local law
The state minimum wage, because state law preempts local minimum wage ordinances

questions.explanation: When federal, state, and local minimum wages all apply, the employee is entitled to the highest. Los Angeles has a city minimum wage above the state rate, and some industries there have even higher rates.

wrongReasons.B: The rate depends on where the work is performed, not where the employer is based.
wrongReasons.C: Federal law sets a floor; a higher state or local rate applies when it exists.
wrongReasons.D: California allows cities to set higher minimum wages, which then apply.

questions.stem: A market survey shows a median of $72,000 for a benchmark job as of January 1 of this year. Salaries in this market are rising 3.5% per year. Age the data to July 1 of this year using simple aging.
questions.explanation: Six months is half a year. Aging factor = 1 + (0.035 × 0.5) = 1.0175. $72,000 × 1.0175 = $73,260.
questions.otherNotes: $74,520 applies the full 3.5% for a whole year. $72,000 fails to age the data.

questions.stem: An employee on FMLA leave who had employer-paid health coverage must have that coverage maintained during the leave on the same terms as if the employee had continued to ________.
questions.explanation: Under the FMLA and CFRA, the employer must maintain group health coverage during leave on the same terms as if the employee were working, including the employer's share of premiums.
