questions.otherNotes: Ending coverage at the start of leave violates the law. Offering COBRA during protected leave is incorrect because there has been no qualifying event.

questions.stem: Which pairing correctly classifies direct and indirect compensation?

choices.text: Direct: health insurance and bonuses; indirect: base salary and tuition assistance
Direct: commissions and overtime pay; indirect: retirement contributions and paid time off
Direct: base salary and paid time off; indirect: incentive pay and life insurance
Direct: disability insurance and wages; indirect: commissions and retirement contributions

questions.explanation: Direct compensation is cash pay for work (wages, overtime, bonuses, commissions, incentives). Indirect compensation is non-cash rewards from employment (health, retirement, paid time off, insurance, tuition assistance).

wrongReasons.A: Health insurance is indirect and base salary is direct.
wrongReasons.C: Paid time off is indirect (pay for time not worked), and incentive pay is direct.
wrongReasons.D: Disability insurance is indirect, and commissions are direct.

questions.stem: Under California's Labor Code, a commission agreement for employees must be in ________ and must describe how commissions will be computed and paid.
questions.explanation: Labor Code section 2751 requires that commission contracts be in writing, set forth the method of computing and paying commissions, and be signed by the employer and the employee, who must receive a signed copy.
questions.otherNotes: Verbal agreements do not satisfy the law. Posting the terms on a bulletin board does not satisfy the requirement for a signed contract.

questions.stem: The CEO wants to replace annual merit increases with one company-wide cost-of-living increase for everyone. Which recommendation is best?

choices.text: Adopt the flat increase, because it is simpler to administer and treats all employees equally
Keep a performance-based element and add structure adjustments when data justify them
Reject the proposal, because general increases weaken the link between pay and performance
Adopt the flat increase and use it to close pay compression for long-tenured employees

questions.explanation: A flat increase is simple and tracks inflation but weakens the pay-for-performance link and ignores role-specific market movement. Keeping a merit or lump-sum component plus data-based structure adjustments balances both.

wrongReasons.A: A flat increase does not differentiate by performance and may drive high performers away.
wrongReasons.C: This ignores the real benefits of simplicity and of keeping pace with inflation.
wrongReasons.D: Equal increases for all do not change relative pay, so they do not fix compression.

questions.stem: Under California's paid sick leave law as amended effective 2024, an employer using the front-loading method must provide at least ________ hours (or five days) of paid sick leave at the start of each year.
questions.explanation: SB 616 increased California's paid sick leave minimum to 40 hours or five days, whichever is greater, per year for employers using front-loading. For accrual, employees accrue at least one hour per 30 hours worked, and employers may cap use at 40 hours or five days per year and total accrual at 80 hours or 10 days.
questions.otherNotes: 24 hours or three days was the prior minimum. 80 hours is the accrual cap, not the front-loaded minimum.

questions.stem: A salesperson earns a base salary of $3,000 per month plus 5% commission on sales above $50,000 per month. This month she sold $110,000. Calculate her total pay for the month.
questions.otherNotes: $8,500 applies the commission to all $110,000 in sales. $3,000 is only the base salary.

questions.stem: Which peer-to-peer recognition design best fits a 500-employee company with a modest budget?

choices.text: Manager-only nominations reviewed quarterly, with the count of awards as the success measure
Unlimited points that employees can give at any time, with total points redeemed as the measure
Monthly point allotments for values-based peer awards, a visible feed, and outcome metrics
An annual peer vote for one employee of the year, with the vote count as the measure

questions.explanation: Effective programs are simple, visible, values-based, and inclusive. A fixed point allotment controls cost, and measuring participation, distribution across groups, engagement items, and retention shows whether it works.

wrongReasons.A: Manager-only recognition is not peer-to-peer and limits reach, and counts alone miss impact on engagement.
wrongReasons.B: Unlimited points remove budget control, and redemptions do not show engagement or retention effects.
wrongReasons.D: An annual award is not timely and recognizes very few people.

questions.stem: Calculate the CEO pay ratio (CEO total compensation to median employee compensation), rounded to the nearest whole number.
questions.explanation: Total CEO compensation = $950,000 + $1,800,000 + $4,200,000 = $6,950,000. Ratio = $6,950,000 / $78,000 ≈ 89.1, or 89:1. Public companies must disclose this ratio under the Dodd-Frank Act.
questions.otherNotes: 12:1 uses only base salary. 35:1 excludes the stock award ($2,750,000 / $78,000).

questions.stem: Which change to the CEO's incentive design best responds to the 58% say-on-pay vote?

choices.text: Make no changes, because the say-on-pay vote is advisory and the proposal still passed
Increase the CEO's base salary and reduce the bonus so that pay depends less on results
Tie more incentive pay to relative TSR with thresholds, and use performance shares
Keep the bonus formula and add a larger grant of time-based restricted stock next year

questions.explanation: A 58% result signals a perceived pay-performance gap. Linking incentives to shareholder-aligned measures with thresholds, using performance-vesting shares, capping payouts, strengthening clawbacks, and engaging shareholders addresses it.

wrongReasons.A: Ignoring a sharply lower vote risks further shareholder opposition and proxy advisor criticism.
wrongReasons.B: Raising fixed pay weakens the pay-performance link and worsens the problem.
wrongReasons.D: Time-based stock rewards tenure, not performance, and does not address the criticism.

questions.stem: The provision that allows a company to recover incentive compensation paid to executives based on financial results that are later restated is called a ________ provision.
questions.explanation: SEC Rule 10D-1 (adopted under the Dodd-Frank Act) requires listed companies to adopt and enforce policies to recover erroneously awarded incentive compensation after an accounting restatement.
questions.otherNotes: A "golden parachute" provides payments upon a change in control. A "vesting" schedule defines when awards become owned.

questions.stem: An employee may contribute to a health savings account (HSA) only if enrolled in a ________ health plan.
questions.explanation: HSA eligibility requires enrollment in a qualifying high-deductible health plan and no disqualifying coverage. HSA funds belong to the employee and roll over year to year. California does not follow federal HSA tax treatment, so contributions are subject to California state income tax.
questions.otherNotes: "PPO" and "HMO" plans are not HSA-eligible unless they meet HDHP requirements. A flexible spending account is a different arrangement.

questions.stem: Match each federal law to its benefits requirement.

prompts.text: Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act

options.text: Allows continuation of group health coverage after a qualifying event
Sets fiduciary, reporting, and disclosure standards for private benefit plans
Protects the privacy of health information and provides special enrollment rights
Requires that pregnancy be treated the same as other medical conditions in benefits
Requires mental health and substance use benefits to be no more restrictive than medical and surgical benefits

questions.explanation: Each law addresses a different aspect of benefit plan design, administration, or protection.
questions.otherNotes: COBRA and HIPAA are often confused. COBRA provides continuation of coverage; HIPAA's privacy rule protects health information held by health plans and providers.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a total rewards statement and how it supports retention?

choices.text: A pay stub that lists gross pay, deductions, and net pay for each pay period
A Form W-2 that reports annual wages and taxes withheld to the employee and the IRS
A benefits enrollment guide that explains plan options and costs during open enrollment
A personalized summary of pay, benefits, and other rewards showing their full value

questions.explanation: Employees often underestimate the value of benefits. A personalized statement of salary, bonuses, employer-paid benefits, retirement contributions, and paid time off increases perceived value and supports retention.

wrongReasons.A: A pay stub shows a single period's pay, not total rewards value.
wrongReasons.B: A W-2 is a tax form and leaves out employer-paid benefits and other rewards.
wrongReasons.C: An enrollment guide explains choices, not the value of the individual's total package.

questions.stem: A company pays software engineers $10,000 more than other employees in the same grade because the market rate for engineers has increased faster than the salary structure. This separate pay adjustment for a specific in-demand job family is called a market ________.
questions.explanation: A market premium or adjustment pays a job family above its grade to reflect external market rates. It should be based on documented market data and reviewed regularly, and it must not create pay differences based on protected characteristics.
questions.otherNotes: "Red circle" rates describe pay above the range maximum. "Green circle" rates describe pay below the minimum. Neither is based on market conditions for a whole job family.

questions.stem: Many employees in their 20s and 30s carry student loans. Which approach to a student loan repayment benefit is best?

choices.text: Adopt the benefit now for all employees, since student debt is common in the workforce
Reject the benefit, since employees without student loans would receive no value from it
Adopt the benefit as taxable cash payments, since loan repayment cannot receive tax-favored treatment
Confirm need with workforce data, then use Section 127 payments or a loan-based 401(k) match

questions.explanation: The decision should weigh workforce needs, equity, tax treatment, and cost. Section 127 excludes up to $5,250 a year (made permanent in 2025), and SECURE 2.0 allows 401(k) matches based on qualified student loan payments.

wrongReasons.A: Adopting without checking workforce data may waste money if few employees carry loans.
wrongReasons.B: Rejecting it ignores targeted value for a large segment of the workforce.
wrongReasons.C: Section 127 excludes up to $5,250 a year of employer loan repayments from income.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 1

questions.stem: Arrange the core steps of the workforce planning process in the correct order.

items.text: Develop and implement action plans to close the gaps
Identify gaps and surpluses by comparing forecast demand to projected supply
Scan the strategic direction and the internal and external environment
Monitor results and revise the plan as conditions change
Forecast future workforce demand and project the supply of current employees

questions.explanation: Planning starts from where the business is going. Demand and supply forecasts are built from that direction (they can be done in parallel, which is why they are one step here). Gaps can be identified only after both are known, action follows the gaps, and monitoring closes the loop.
questions.otherNotes: Writing action plans before the gap analysis leads to hiring or layoffs based on assumption. Treating monitoring as the first step gives nothing to monitor against.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 1

questions.stem: The total package of rewards, opportunities, and experiences an organization offers in exchange for employees' skills and commitment is its employee ________ proposition (EVP).
questions.explanation: The EVP is the "give and get" that makes the organization attractive to candidates and employees. It anchors employer branding and recruiting messages.
questions.otherNotes: "Valuation" and "verification" are not part of the term. An EVP is not a compensation philosophy alone; it includes culture, growth, and work environment.

source.doc: Workforce Planning and Talent Acquisition Worksheet 1

questions.stem: A 400-employee company's largest customer, 30% of revenue, may not renew in six months. About 120 employees work on the account, and skilled roles take about five months to fill. Which workforce planning approach is best?

choices.text: Hire ahead now for the renewal scenario so that skilled roles are filled before the decision
Lay off the account team now so that costs are already reduced before the decision arrives
Plan renew and non-renew scenarios with triggers, cross-train staff, and use contingent labor
Keep current staffing unchanged and decide on workforce actions once the customer decides

questions.explanation: Because hiring lead time nearly matches the decision window, the plan must keep flexibility and avoid irreversible commitments: scenarios with triggers, cross-training, contingent labor, redeployment paths, and a prepared (not launched) WARN-compliant reduction plan.

questions.explanation: Cascading with cross-functional alignment resolves conflicts while keeping goals relevant to each unit.
questions.stem: Company strategy targets 15% growth in recurring revenue, but each unit sets its own goals and several conflict. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Tie bonuses to individual goals so that employees focus on their own contributions
Let each unit continue setting its own goals and resolve conflicts as they surface during the year
Cascade enterprise objectives to teams, hold alignment sessions across functions, and show linkages
Assign the same growth goal to each unit so that teams pursue common targets across the company

wrongReasons.A: Individual-only incentives can intensify conflicts across units.
wrongReasons.B: Independent goals produced the current conflicts.
wrongReasons.D: Identical goals ignore differing contributions.

questions.explanation: A missed meal period requires one hour of premium pay per workday, and a missed rest period requires a separate premium.
questions.stem: On a day Dana works an 8.5-hour shift without any meal period and without a valid waiver, what premium does California law require?

choices.text: One and one-half hours of pay at her regular rate of compensation for the missed period
Thirty minutes of pay at her regular rate for the length of the missed meal period
A premium is not owed if she chose to keep working through the meal period
One additional hour of pay at her regular rate of compensation for that workday

wrongReasons.A: The premium is one hour, not 1.5 hours.
wrongReasons.B: The premium is a full hour, not the length of the meal period.
wrongReasons.C: A valid waiver is required; choosing to work through an unprovided meal period does not excuse the premium.

questions.explanation: Reporting-time pay guarantees half of the scheduled day, here three hours, with a floor of two and a cap of four; 3 x $20 = $60.
questions.stem: Dana is scheduled for six hours, reports for work, and is sent home after one hour. Under the California wage order for retail, what is the minimum total pay owed for that day?

wrongReasons.A: Twenty dollars pays only the hour worked.
wrongReasons.B: Forty dollars applies the two-hour floor, which is below half of the scheduled six hours.
wrongReasons.D: Eighty dollars applies the four-hour cap, which would apply only to a scheduled shift of eight hours or more.

questions.explanation: California applies a control test, so mandatory exit searches are hours worked, unlike under the federal Portal-to-Portal Act.
questions.stem: Under California law, how is the time Dana spends waiting for and completing the post-shift bag check treated?

choices.text: Not compensable, because the activity occurs after she has clocked out for the day
Compensable hours worked because she remains under the employer's control
Not compensable, because the federal rule treats exit screening as a postliminary activity
Compensable if it exceeds 15 minutes, since shorter periods are treated as minimal

wrongReasons.A: Clocking out does not end employer control.
wrongReasons.C: The federal approach does not govern California's more protective rule.
wrongReasons.D: California has no 15-minute threshold for this time.

questions.explanation: Successor employers may treat retained workers as continuing employees and assume the seller's forms and any errors, or complete new forms.
questions.stem: A buyer acquires a company's assets and keeps all its workers. What are its options for the existing Forms I-9?

choices.text: Complete new Forms I-9 for the retained employees, or keep the seller's forms and accept any errors
Skip Forms I-9 for retained employees because they were verified at their original hire
Complete new Forms I-9 for the retained employees on the closing date and then destroy the seller's forms
Leave the liability for errors in the seller's forms with the seller after closing

wrongReasons.B: Retained employees are still subject to verification requirements.
wrongReasons.C: The rules allow retaining the predecessor's forms.
wrongReasons.D: Successor liability for the assumed forms transfers to the buyer.

questions.explanation: Kotter's sequence begins with urgency, then coalition, then vision, then broad enlistment, then removing obstacles.
questions.stem: Arrange these steps from Kotter's change model in their intended order.

items.text: Build a guiding coalition
Create a sense of urgency
Enlist a volunteer army
Form a strategic vision
Enable action by removing barriers

questions.explanation: Impact and replaceability identify the roles whose vacancy would hurt the business most.
questions.stem: Which approach best selects roles for succession planning so that it protects business continuity?

choices.text: Rank roles by business impact if vacant and difficulty to replace, regardless of level or title
Include roles held by the longest-tenured employees, because they are closest to retirement
Include each role at director level and above, because those roles carry the most authority
Include roles that executives nominate, because they know which positions matter most

wrongReasons.B: Tenure indicates retirement risk, not criticality.
wrongReasons.C: Level alone misses critical technical or specialist roles.
wrongReasons.D: Nominations introduce bias and omit critical roles.

questions.explanation: Credible pay data are large, current, and matched on job content; older data should be aged to the effective date before use.
questions.stem: Three surveys put the median pay for a Senior Data Engineer in San Jose at $168,000, $181,000, and $149,000. The $149,000 survey has 14 participants and matches jobs by title only. The $181,000 survey has 220 participants, matches by duties and level, and was published five months ago. The $168,000 survey has 60 participants, matches by duties, and uses data 20 months old. Which approach best builds the market reference?

choices.text: Use the lowest median to control cost until the company confirms what the market is paying
Weight the large, current, duties-matched survey most heavily and age the older data before blending
Use the highest median so that the company stays competitive for scarce data engineering talent
Average the three medians equally so that the differences among the surveys offset one another

wrongReasons.A: Using the lowest figure relies on the weakest data and risks attrition.
wrongReasons.C: Using the highest figure ignores data quality and may overspend.
wrongReasons.D: Equal weighting gives a thin, title-matched sample the same influence as a robust one.

questions.explanation: Payments routed to a personal account with a stated link to officials are classic red flags that require immediate escalation to legal and compliance.
questions.stem: A U.S. company's sales agent in a foreign country asks for a $40,000 consulting fee wired to a personal account, saying it will help with licensing officials. How should the CHRO, as owner of the ethics program, respond?

choices.text: Approve it because the amount falls below the company's threshold for facilitating payments
Pay half now and half after the license issues to limit the company's exposure
Approve it after the agent provides a written assurance that officials will not receive funds
Stop the payment and refer the request to legal and compliance for review under the FCPA

wrongReasons.A: The FCPA's narrow facilitating-payment exception does not cover discretionary licensing decisions, and a $40,000 transfer is not routine.
wrongReasons.B: Splitting the payment does not change its purpose or the liability.
wrongReasons.C: A self-serving written assurance does not cure the red flags and does not satisfy due diligence.

questions.explanation: The evidence points to usability problems, which are fixed by task-based redesign and user testing.
questions.stem: Six months after launching employee self-service, only 30% of employees use it, call volume to HR is unchanged, and a survey shows employees cannot find the forms they need. Which action is best?

choices.text: Add more features to the portal so that it covers a wider range of HR transactions and forms
Mandate self-service use and discipline employees who continue to call HR with routine questions
Redesign navigation and search around top tasks, test with employees, and retire duplicate channels
Cancel the project and return to handling employee requests by email and telephone as before

wrongReasons.A: More features add complexity to a portal that employees already cannot navigate.
wrongReasons.B: Discipline addresses compliance, not the usability barrier.
wrongReasons.D: Reverting forfeits efficiency gains that a redesign can unlock.

questions.explanation: A stock purchase transfers all liabilities, so unquantified legal exposure pushes buyers toward an asset purchase.
questions.stem: Due diligence on a California manufacturer reveals an unquantified exposure from a pending class action over unpaid meal and rest premiums. Which finding most strongly favors structuring the deal as an asset purchase rather than a stock purchase?

choices.text: Differences in handbook formatting, because the policies must be reconciled
The wage-and-hour class action, because its exposure cannot yet be quantified
The absence of a formal recognition program, because it weakens engagement
Turnover in the sales group, because it runs well above the market average

wrongReasons.A: Formatting differences are a cosmetic integration issue.
wrongReasons.C: Recognition programs are not a liability driver.
wrongReasons.D: Turnover affects value but not deal structure in this way.

questions.stem: A leadership program costs $90,000. In the first year, it produced $120,000 in measurable productivity gains and $24,000 in avoided error costs. What is the training ROI, using ROI% = (benefits - costs) / costs x 100? Enter the percentage.

questions.explanation: The deal's value depends on retaining specific talent, so retention drivers and role clarity come before broad harmonization.
questions.stem: Which action should HR prioritize in the first 100 days?

choices.text: Harmonize the HR policies and pay structures of both companies as quickly as the integration timeline allows
Delay communication to employees until the final integration plan has been approved by the board
Move Brightpath into NovaTech's performance management system to ensure consistency across the combined company
Identify critical talent and retention drivers, then deploy targeted retention agreements and role communication

wrongReasons.A: Immediate harmonization risks unsettling the people the deal depends on.
wrongReasons.B: Silence during integration drives rumors and attrition.
wrongReasons.C: A forced system change is disruptive without addressing retention.

questions.explanation: Consistent exit themes about approvals and authority point to clashing norms for how decisions are made.
questions.stem: Within weeks, Brightpath engineers resign at three times NovaTech's rate. Exit interviews cite approval layers and unclear decision authority. What does this most strongly indicate?

choices.text: A culture mismatch in decision rights that the integration plan has not addressed
A pay gap between the two companies that leadership must close at once
Normal post-merger attrition that does not call for a management response
A weak labor market for engineers that is pulling employees to other employers

wrongReasons.B: Exit interviews did not cite pay as the cause.
wrongReasons.C: Attrition at triple the baseline rate is not normal and signals a problem.
wrongReasons.D: Nothing in the facts suggests labor-market conditions.

questions.explanation: Co-designing decision rights gives needed governance while preserving autonomy where it drives value.
questions.stem: Leadership wants to address the mismatch. Which approach best balances integration with the autonomy the engineers value?

choices.text: Impose NovaTech's approval matrix immediately across Brightpath and relax it after the transition settles
Define which decisions need central approval and which stay with the product team, co-designed with Brightpath
Hold a values workshop with both teams while leaving the approval structure and reporting lines unchanged
Leave Brightpath fully separate from NovaTech's governance and decision processes for the foreseeable future

wrongReasons.A: Imposing the matrix first accelerates attrition.
wrongReasons.C: A workshop without structural change does not resolve the decision-rights problem.
wrongReasons.D: Indefinite separation forfeits integration benefits.

questions.explanation: An adverse-impact review before notices go out identifies and addresses discriminatory patterns while the plan can still change.
questions.stem: A company plans a reduction in force. Preliminary analysis shows that selecting by recent performance ratings disproportionately selects workers over 50. What is the best next step?

choices.text: Run an adverse-impact analysis by age and other protected groups, and validate the criteria
Skip the analysis to keep the process confidential until notices are delivered
Finalize the list because performance ratings are objective measures of employee contribution
Switch to selecting by lowest salary, which avoids reliance on subjective ratings

wrongReasons.B: Confidentiality does not justify skipping a legal risk review.
wrongReasons.C: Ratings can embed bias and still produce adverse impact.
wrongReasons.D: Selecting by salary also tends to affect older workers disproportionately.

questions.explanation: Role-level supply modeling against demand shows where and when the shortfall will occur and how large it will be.
questions.stem: A utility's analytics show 35% of line-crew supervisors will be retirement-eligible within three years while apprenticeship completions are flat. Which analysis best supports planning?

choices.text: An engagement survey of supervisors that measures their commitment to the company and its mission
A salary comparison for apprentices against market rates for similar programs in the region
Retirement-eligibility and pipeline-conversion analysis by critical role against projected demand
A company-wide average-age report showing the age distribution of the supervisor workforce

wrongReasons.A: Engagement does not quantify the supply gap.
wrongReasons.B: Pay comparisons do not size the pipeline problem.
wrongReasons.D: An average age hides role-level exposure and timing.

questions.explanation: Weingarten covers investigatory interviews, the duty of fair representation binds unions, past practice can acquire contractual force, and arbitration resolves disputes through a neutral. A lockout is the employer's economic weapon, not any of these four.
questions.stem: Match each labor relations concept to its description.

options.text: An employer's temporary withholding of work to pressure the union
A represented employee's right to request a representative at an investigatory interview that could lead to discipline
A union's obligation to represent all bargaining-unit members without hostility or arbitrariness
A consistent, long-standing practice that can become an implied term of the relationship
Final resolution of a contract dispute by a neutral third party

questions.note: Each option is used at most once; one option is not used.

questions.explanation: Sutures are medical treatment beyond first aid, so the case is recordable.
questions.stem: A safety manager is deciding which work-related cases must be entered on the OSHA 300 log. Which case is recordable?

choices.text: An employee receives a tetanus booster after a work-related cut
An employee takes nonprescription ibuprofen at nonprescription strength after a strain
An employee has a work-related wound cleaned and covered with a bandage
An employee receives sutures to close a laceration

wrongReasons.A: A tetanus booster is listed as first aid.
wrongReasons.B: Nonprescription medication at nonprescription strength is first aid.
wrongReasons.C: Cleaning and bandaging a wound is first aid.

questions.explanation: Wage discussions are protected concerted activity, and California separately bars pay-secrecy rules and retaliation.
questions.stem: A handbook prohibits employees from discussing pay, and a manager disciplines a California employee who shared her salary with coworkers. What is the most accurate assessment?

choices.text: The rule is lawful as long as it exempts supervisors from the restriction
The rule and discipline are unlawful because employees may discuss their wages
The rule is lawful because pay data are confidential business information of the employer
The rule is lawful as long as the employer applies it equally to each employee

wrongReasons.A: Excluding supervisors does not make a rule against nonsupervisory employees lawful.
wrongReasons.C: Wage information employees hold about themselves is not an employer trade secret.
wrongReasons.D: Equal application does not cure an unlawful restraint.

questions.explanation: Prepared managers, repeated multichannel messaging, and feedback loops reduce uncertainty and surface resistance early.
questions.stem: Which TWO practices most improve adoption when leaders announce a restructuring? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Repeat the core message through several channels and test understanding with pulse checks
Send one comprehensive CEO email and avoid follow-up to limit rumors
Equip managers with talking points and a feedback channel before the broad announcement
Share information only with directly affected employees
Wait to announce until every detail is final, even if rumors circulate

wrongReasons.B: One message with no follow-up leaves questions unanswered and rumors uncorrected.
wrongReasons.D: Limiting information to the affected group fuels fear among everyone else.
wrongReasons.E: Silence while rumors circulate erodes trust and invites speculation.

questions.explanation: White pass rate = 70%; Hispanic pass rate = 50%; 50 / 70 = 71%, below the 80% guideline, which signals adverse impact requiring justification.
questions.stem: What do the pass rates indicate under the four-fifths guideline?

choices.text: Unlawful discrimination has been established because the Hispanic pass rate is below the white pass rate
Adverse impact is indicated when the lower pass rate is above 80% of the higher pass rate
Adverse impact is indicated because the Hispanic pass rate is about 71% of the white pass rate, below 80%
Adverse impact is absent because the pass rates for both groups are at or above 50%

wrongReasons.A: The guideline indicates potential adverse impact, not proof of discrimination.
wrongReasons.B: A ratio below 80% indicates adverse impact; above 80% generally does not.
wrongReasons.D: The comparison is between groups' rates, not an absolute floor.

questions.explanation: When a selection procedure shows adverse impact, the employer must demonstrate job-relatedness and consider alternatives with less impact.
questions.stem: What is the best next step regarding the test?

choices.text: Conduct a validation study showing job-relatedness and evaluate less adverse alternatives
Continue using the test unchanged because the four-fifths guideline is not itself a law
Raise the Hispanic applicants' scores so that the pass rates for the two groups are equalized
Stop recording applicant demographics so that future pass-rate comparisons cannot be made

wrongReasons.B: The guideline is an enforcement rule of thumb, and disparate impact liability is statutory.
wrongReasons.C: Adjusting scores by group is prohibited by Title VII.
wrongReasons.D: Stopping data collection hides the problem and violates recordkeeping duties.

questions.explanation: The pay scale must reflect a good-faith estimate, and salary-history inquiries are prohibited.
questions.stem: Under California law, which assessment of the posting and recruiter practice is most accurate?

choices.text: The posted range is lawful because it includes the highest amount the company might pay for the role
Pay ranges are required for applicants who ask for them, but not in the job posting itself
Asking about current pay is lawful if the candidate is told that answering is voluntary
The range must be a good-faith estimate, and employers may not ask applicants about salary history

wrongReasons.A: The 2026 amendments require a good-faith estimate, not a theoretical maximum.
wrongReasons.B: Employers with 15 or more employees must include the range in postings.
wrongReasons.C: The prohibition on asking is not cured by allowing the candidate to decline.

questions.explanation: Title VII covers 15 or more employees, the ADEA 20 or more, FMLA 50 or more within 75 miles, and CFRA 5 or more. The 100-employee figure is the federal WARN and EEO-1 threshold.
questions.stem: Match each statute to the minimum employer size that triggers coverage.

options.text: 20 or more employees
50 or more employees within 75 miles
15 or more employees
100 or more employees
5 or more employees

questions.note: Each option is used at most once; one option is not used.

questions.explanation: Criteria that function as age proxies can produce adverse impact and disparate treatment under the ADEA and FEHA.
questions.stem: A talent review's 9-box places 90% of 'high-potential' ratings on employees under 40, because potential was defined as 'energy and a long career runway.' Which concern matters most?

choices.text: The 9-box should be replaced with a seniority list because tenure is an objective measure
Age-discrimination exposure from criteria that proxy for age, so potential needs job-related criteria
The performance axis creates the legal risk, while the potential axis is a neutral assessment
Little concern, because potential is a subjective judgment that discrimination laws do not cover

wrongReasons.A: A seniority list ignores capability and creates its own problems.
wrongReasons.C: The potential axis, as defined, is the source of the age-related risk.
wrongReasons.D: Subjective criteria are still subject to discrimination laws.

questions.explanation: Personalized, complete figures make the full value of rewards visible.
questions.stem: Which feature most improves the perceived value of an individual total rewards statement?

choices.text: A statement that lists base pay and the date of the employee's next pay review
A statement prepared for executives that summarizes their incentive compensation
Showing employer-paid benefit costs, retirement contributions, and equity alongside base pay
A generic brochure that describes the programs available to the workforce in general terms

wrongReasons.A: Base pay alone hides most of the employer's investment.
wrongReasons.B: Limiting it to executives omits those whose perception matters for retention.
wrongReasons.D: Generic descriptions lack individual figures.

questions.explanation: California requires employers to reimburse necessary business expenses incurred in the discharge of duties.
questions.stem: A California company adopts hybrid scheduling, and employees report using personal phones and home internet for work. Which design element is both required in California and supportive of equity?

choices.text: Offer a flat stipend to employees who ask for help with their phone and internet costs
Prohibit the use of personal devices and home internet for work activity
Let employees absorb the costs as a trade-off for the flexibility of hybrid scheduling
Reimburse a reasonable share of necessary business expenses such as phone and internet costs

wrongReasons.A: A stipend limited to those who ask creates inequity and may leave expenses unreimbursed.
wrongReasons.B: A prohibition does not address the expense obligation where devices are needed.
wrongReasons.C: Employees cannot absorb required business expenses.

questions.explanation: Replacement cost per separation = 1.5 x 60,000 = $90,000. Avoided separations = 8, so savings = 8 x 90,000 = $720,000. Net benefit = 720,000 - 520,000 = $200,000.
questions.stem: Replacing a separated employee costs 1.5 times annual salary, and the average salary is $60,000. A retention program costing $520,000 is projected to cut annual separations from 30 to 22. What is the projected first-year net benefit in dollars?

questions.explanation: Employer-sponsored groups must be open to all employees to avoid discrimination in participation and access to development.
questions.stem: An employee resource group for Black employees is open to all, but its manager tells an Asian employee who asked to join that the group is not for him. What is the best HR response?

choices.text: Confirm that membership is open to all employees and coach the manager and group leaders
Support the manager because affinity groups are permitted to limit their membership
Close the group until a new charter is written and approved by senior leadership
Tell the employee to start a separate group that reflects his own background

wrongReasons.B: Employer-sponsored groups cannot exclude by protected characteristic.
wrongReasons.C: Closing the group is a disproportionate response to a correctable error.
wrongReasons.D: Redirecting the employee leaves the exclusion in place.

questions.explanation: Migration quality depends on clean, governed source data and parallel testing, especially for payroll.
questions.stem: During a pilot of a new HRIS, 12% of employee records show mismatched job codes and duplicate entries. Which action should occur before go-live?

choices.text: Limit the new system to recruiting and leave payroll and employee data in the legacy system for now
Delete the duplicate records without review so that the data set looks clean at cutover and during testing
Go live as planned and correct the data errors over the following year while employees keep using the system
Establish data governance: cleanse source data, assign ownership, and run parallel payroll tests before cutover

wrongReasons.A: Limiting scope sidesteps the data problem rather than solving it.
wrongReasons.B: Deleting without review risks losing valid history.
wrongReasons.C: Live errors in payroll and compliance data carry legal and trust costs.

questions.explanation: Training that is mandatory and directly job-related is working time even when held outside regular hours.
questions.stem: A nonexempt employee must attend a job-related certification course after her regular shift. Attendance is mandatory, and she performs no other work during it. Under the FLSA, how is the time treated?

choices.text: It is not compensable because it occurs outside the employee's regular working hours
It is compensable hours worked because attendance is mandatory and directly job-related
It is not compensable because she earns a certificate that benefits her career
It is compensable if total hours worked during the week exceed 40

wrongReasons.A: After-hours timing alone does not make mandatory job-related training noncompensable.
wrongReasons.C: A certificate does not change the classification of required training.
wrongReasons.D: Compensability does not depend on weekly hours; overtime is a separate question.

citations: Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code 3300 et seq.
questions.explanation: Paid Family Leave is a wage-replacement benefit administered by the state, separate from the leave statutes that protect jobs.
questions.stem: Which statement about California Paid Family Leave is correct?

choices.text: It is funded by employers through a payroll tax that is assessed on company wages each quarter
It applies to employees of employers that have 50 or more workers within 75 miles of the worksite
It provides partial wage replacement through state disability insurance for up to eight weeks
It guarantees reinstatement to the same job at the end of the leave period of up to eight weeks

wrongReasons.B: It is available to covered employees regardless of employer size.
wrongReasons.D: Job protection is not a feature of the wage-replacement program.

questions.explanation: HR strategy is derived from business strategy, so the capability gap must be defined before talent programs are designed or funded.
questions.stem: A regional healthcare network will shift 40% of its revenue from inpatient care to outpatient and telehealth services over three years. The CHRO has been asked to produce the HR strategy. Which action should come first?

choices.text: Redesign the performance review form to emphasize digital and telehealth competencies for clinical staff
Launch an enterprise reskilling program across clinical roles to prepare staff for outpatient and telehealth work
Assess the gap between current workforce capabilities and the capabilities the new service mix will require
Benchmark compensation against outpatient competitors so the rewards budget reflects the new service mix

wrongReasons.B: Reskilling everyone before the gap is sized wastes spend on skills that may already exist or may not be needed.
wrongReasons.D: Pay benchmarking is a downstream rewards decision that depends on which roles and skills the new model needs.
wrongReasons.A: Form redesign is a tactical tool change; it does not establish what capabilities must be built.

questions.stem: In Kirkpatrick's evaluation model, which level measures whether participants apply what they learned on the job?

choices.text: Level 3: Behavior
Level 2: Learning
Level 1: Reaction
Level 4: Results

wrongReasons.D: Level 4 measures organizational outcomes.
wrongReasons.C: Level 1 measures participant satisfaction.

questions.explanation: California requires a salary of at least twice the state minimum wage for full-time work, so a $62,000 salary fails the state test.
questions.stem: A Texas-based retailer employs an assistant store manager in California on a $62,000 salary. She directs two employees and spends about 60% of her time on exempt managerial work. Under federal and California law as of December 2026, how should she be classified?

choices.text: Nonexempt for overtime purposes but exempt from the meal and rest period rules that apply to managers
Exempt, because California applies a duties test and sets no separate salary minimum for managers
Exempt, because the federal salary and duties tests are satisfied and federal law controls the outcome
Nonexempt, because her $62,000 salary is below California's $70,304 minimum, though above the federal level

wrongReasons.A: Nonexempt status carries overtime and meal and rest period protections together.
wrongReasons.C: Federal law sets a floor and does not preempt the higher California standard.
wrongReasons.B: California requires both a salary minimum and a duties test.

questions.explanation: A low response rate raises nonresponse bias, so findings need representativeness checks and triangulation before a major decision.
questions.stem: An engagement survey of 1,200 employees drew a 22% response rate, and leadership wants to restructure the call-center shift model based on it. What is the best use of the data?

choices.text: Treat results as directional, test them for representativeness, and validate with focus groups and operational data
Proceed with the restructuring because 264 responses exceed the minimum needed for statistical significance
Rerun the survey with mandatory participation so that the full workforce is represented
Discard the survey results and rely on manager observations of the call-center shift pattern

wrongReasons.B: Sample size alone does not remove nonresponse bias.
wrongReasons.C: Mandatory participation undermines candor and trust.
wrongReasons.D: Discarding data in favor of anecdote is less credible, not more.

questions.explanation: California permits only specified, job-related reasons for pay differences and requires multi-year recordkeeping.
questions.stem: Which TWO practices comply with California's Equal Pay Act when setting pay? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Keep job title and wage rate records for each employee for the duration of employment plus three years
Apply equal pay rules only to workers in identical jobs at the same site
Justify pay differences by pointing to each employee's prior salary
Prohibit employees from asking coworkers about pay if the rule applies to everyone
Explain pay differences by a seniority system, merit system, production-based system, or a bona fide job-related factor consistent with business necessity

wrongReasons.B: California covers substantially similar work, not only identical jobs.
wrongReasons.C: Prior salary cannot justify a pay difference under California law.
wrongReasons.D: California bars rules that prevent employees from discussing pay.

A plan that the employer must prepare after a violent incident has occurred at the workplace
A written workplace violence prevention plan, annual training, and a violent incident log
A federal OSHA standard that preempts the state rule and sets the plan's content

questions.stem: A firm has 40 senior engineers. This year 6 will retire, 4 will move into management, and 5 are expected to resign. Three internal engineers are ready to be promoted into senior roles. Demand will rise to 48 senior engineers. How many senior engineers must be hired externally?

wrongReasons.A: Eight counts only net growth and ignores attrition.

questions.explanation: A policy and equity review addresses the structural cause and protects internal mobility and retention.
questions.stem: Internally promoted employees receive 4% increases while external hires into the same grade are brought in 12% higher, creating compression. What is the best response?

choices.text: Tell promoted employees to negotiate their own increases with their managers after promotion
Review promotion-increase guidelines, analyze internal versus external pay equity, and correct compression
Freeze external offers until the pay of internal employees catches up with the pay of new hires
Stop hiring externally into the grade until the internal pay gap closes on its own over time

citations: Ames v. Ohio Dept. of Youth Services (2025)
questions.explanation: Allocating opportunities by race is disparate treatment under Title VII, and Ames confirms all plaintiffs face the same standard.
questions.stem: In 2025 the U.S. Supreme Court held in Ames v. Ohio Department of Youth Services that majority-group Title VII plaintiffs need not meet a heightened evidentiary standard. An employer's leadership program reserves half its seats for employees of specified racial groups. Which federal-law assessment is most accurate?

choices.text: The program creates legal risk mainly among employees in the groups that receive the reserved seats

questions.explanation: Criteria, documentation, and auditing address both bias and consistency while preserving the program's value.
questions.stem: A spot-bonus program lets managers choose recipients. Data show men receive 70% of awards though they are 50% of staff. What is the best response?

choices.text: Leave decisions to managers' discretion because they know their teams' work best and see results first
Cap awards at one per person per year so that distribution is spread more widely across teams
Replace the awards with a team celebration that includes the whole department and its leadership
Define criteria tied to behaviors, require documentation, guide managers, and audit awards by group

wrongReasons.A: Unstructured discretion produced the disparity.
wrongReasons.B: A cap does not address who receives awards.
wrongReasons.C: Eliminating recognition removes a retention tool without fixing the process.

questions.explanation: Developmental use, rater anonymity, and coaching encourage candid ratings and learning.
questions.stem: An organization uses 360-degree feedback. Which practice best protects its validity and developmental value?

choices.text: Let raters sign their comments so that managers know the source of each comment they receive
Use the results to determine bonuses and promotions so that feedback carries real consequences for managers
Use results for development only, aggregate rater groups of three or more, and pair results with coaching
Give the raw results to the employee's manager to use in the next performance review

wrongReasons.A: Identifiable comments discourage candor.
wrongReasons.B: High-stakes use encourages rater inflation and gaming.
wrongReasons.D: Raw results without coaching limit usefulness and may be misused.

questions.explanation: The temporary employee-data exemption expired on January 1, 2023, so covered businesses owe employees notices and rights.
questions.stem: A California company with $60 million in annual revenue collects employee data, including biometric timeclock scans and health information. Which action best aligns HR with the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA in 2026?

choices.text: Provide the notice to job applicants, because they are the consumers the law was written to protect
Collect biometric data without notice because the handbook says employees consent to monitoring
Take no action, because the CPRA exempts employee and job applicant data from its requirements
Give employees a notice at collection listing categories, purposes, and retention, and honor rights requests

wrongReasons.A: Applicants and employees are both covered consumers.
wrongReasons.B: A general handbook clause does not replace the required notice at collection, especially for sensitive data.
wrongReasons.C: The exemption for employee and applicant data ended.

questions.explanation: A trigger-based plan covering safety, communication, and continuity lets leadership act proportionately as conditions change.
questions.stem: A U.S. company employs 120 people in a region where armed conflict risk is rising. The board asks HR what to contribute first. Which element is most important?

choices.text: Termination notices to regional staff to reduce the company's legal and financial exposure
A hazard-pay differential paid to each employee in the region while conditions remain unsettled
A tiered contingency plan with triggers for employee safety, communication, and critical work continuity
Immediate relocation of the entire regional staff to the United States under temporary work visas

wrongReasons.A: Terminations abandon duty-of-care obligations and destroy capability.
wrongReasons.B: A pay differential does not protect people or preserve operations.
wrongReasons.D: Mass relocation is impractical, costly, and ignores varying risk levels.

questions.explanation: Referrals offer fast, low-cost fit; executive search handles confidential senior roles; campus programs build pipelines; internal posting supports mobility. Mass job-board posting is the high-volume hourly option.
questions.stem: Match each recruiting source to the purpose it best serves.

options.text: Reaching high-volume hourly applicants with minimal screening
Building an early-career pipeline and employer brand
Supporting career mobility and retention of current staff
Low-cost access to culturally aligned candidates with faster time to fill
Confidential recruitment of senior leaders from competitors

questions.note: Each option is used at most once; one option is not used.

questions.explanation: Broad on-the-job exposure with structure builds cross-functional capability.
questions.stem: Which assignment best prepares high-potential managers for general management?

choices.text: Shadowing the CEO for a day to observe how senior decisions are made
A cross-functional stretch rotation with a mentor and defined learning objectives
A classroom course on business strategy delivered by an outside university faculty
A lateral move within the same function to deepen the manager's technical expertise

wrongReasons.A: A one-day shadow experience is too brief to build capability.
wrongReasons.C: A course alone provides knowledge but little practice.
wrongReasons.D: A same-function move adds little breadth.

questions.explanation: Manager capability and workload design address both the early-warning and root-cause sides of psychosocial risk.
questions.stem: A company treats employee mental health as a human capital risk after burnout-related absence rose in two departments. Which TWO actions most directly address that risk? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Review workload and staffing data in the high-burnout units and adjust capacity
Train managers to recognize distress and route employees to the EAP and leave options
Subscribe to a wellness app without reviewing workload data
Require employees returning from absence to disclose their diagnosis to HR
Hold a company-wide mindfulness week

wrongReasons.C: An app deployed without workload analysis treats symptoms and ignores root causes.
wrongReasons.D: Requiring diagnosis disclosure invites ADA and privacy problems and discourages help-seeking.
wrongReasons.E: A one-week event is a low-impact gesture with no structural effect.

questions.explanation: Treating contractors like employees on a supervised schedule strengthens a misclassification claim and can expose the employer to claims for plan benefits.
questions.stem: A California firm offers its equity plan and group health coverage to long-term 1099 engineers who work set schedules under direct supervision, hoping to attract talent. What is the greatest risk?

choices.text: The treatment supports employee status under the ABC test and may create plan-eligibility claims
Current employees may become less engaged when contractors receive the same benefits they do
Payroll taxes on the equity grants will rise because contractors receive stock awards
The offer carries little risk, because benefits are voluntary and contractors may decline them

wrongReasons.B: Peer perception is a minor concern compared with legal exposure.
wrongReasons.C: Payroll tax impact is secondary to the classification risk.
wrongReasons.D: Voluntary offers do not override the control facts that decide status.

questions.explanation: Vacancies = 14. Turnover replacement = 0.12 x 600 = 72. New positions = 0.05 x 600 = 30. Total hires = 14 + 72 + 30 = 116.
questions.stem: A hospital has 600 filled registered-nurse positions and 14 approved vacancies. Next year it expects 12% turnover on filled positions (retirements included) and plans 5% growth, measured on the 600 filled positions. How many nurses must it hire next year?

questions.explanation: Concentrated attrition calls for targeted diagnosis rather than broad interventions.
questions.stem: Voluntary turnover is 22%, but 70% of leavers have under one year of tenure and 80% come from two roles. Which action is best?

choices.text: Launch an enterprise-wide engagement initiative that applies to the whole workforce
Target the early-tenure and two-role segments with root-cause work on onboarding and pay
Raise pay across the company to bring pay in line with the labor market for similar roles
Accept 22% as normal for the industry and monitor the rate through the rest of the year

wrongReasons.A: A broad initiative dilutes resources.
wrongReasons.C: An across-the-board raise is costly and untargeted.
wrongReasons.D: Acceptance ignores a concentrated, fixable problem.

questions.explanation: California requires commission agreements to be in writing, specifying the method of computation and payment, with employees receiving a signed copy.
questions.stem: A California employer pays salespeople on commission. Which requirement applies?

choices.text: A verbal agreement that the sales manager documents in the manager's notes and shares with the employee
A written plan summary that is posted internally and updated each year, if commissions are paid on time
A published policy that employees acknowledge through their continued employment with the company
A signed written contract stating how commissions are computed and paid, with a copy for the employee

wrongReasons.A: A verbal agreement does not meet the writing requirement.
wrongReasons.B: Timely payment does not replace the writing requirement.
wrongReasons.C: Implied acknowledgment is not a signed contract.

questions.explanation: High-power, low-interest stakeholders are kept satisfied without overloading them with detail.
questions.stem: A stakeholder has high power but low interest in an HR initiative. According to the power-interest grid, what engagement approach is recommended?

choices.text: Keep satisfied
Keep informed
Monitor
Manage closely

wrongReasons.B: Keep informed applies to low power and high interest.
wrongReasons.C: Monitor applies to low power and low interest.
wrongReasons.D: Manage closely applies to high power and high interest.

questions.explanation: Unilateral changes to mandatory subjects without notice and an opportunity to bargain are unfair labor practices.
questions.stem: A unionized hospital plans to change its attendance policy, a mandatory subject of bargaining under the NLRA. The collective bargaining agreement is silent on attendance and has no management-rights clause covering it. What should HR do before implementing the change?

choices.text: Apply the new policy to nonunion staff and leave the bargaining unit out of it
Implement the change now and bargain with the union if it objects to the new attendance policy
Give the union notice and an opportunity to bargain over the change and its effects before implementing
Implement the change after counsel approves the policy language and senior management signs off on it

wrongReasons.A: Changing terms only for nonunion staff does not avoid bargaining over unit employees' policy.
wrongReasons.B: Implementing first violates the duty to bargain regardless of later bargaining.
wrongReasons.D: Counsel review does not substitute for the bargaining obligation.

questions.explanation: An employer must provide the claim form within one working day of learning of an injury or a claim.
questions.stem: A California supervisor learns today that an employee hurt his back lifting a box at work. What must the employer do within one working day?

choices.text: Give the employee the workers' compensation claim form, whether or not liability is certain
Deny the claim until medical evidence supports that the injury occurred at work
Wait for a physician's report before taking steps to start the claim process
File the claim with the insurer's medical provider network and notify the employee later

wrongReasons.B: Employers cannot discourage or deny claim forms; compensability decisions come from the insurer.
wrongReasons.C: The obligation is triggered by knowledge, not a physician's report.
wrongReasons.D: The form goes to the employee; filing is the employee's act.

citations: Cal. Lab. Code 245-249 (Healthy Workplaces, Healthy Families Act)
questions.explanation: A principles-plus-addenda design keeps consistency in intent while complying locally and honoring the funding constraint.
questions.stem: A manufacturer has sites in Texas, Ohio, and California and wants one consistent sick-leave and attendance experience. Leadership will fund benefits at the legal minimum at each site. Which approach best aligns HR strategy across locations?

choices.text: Apply California's requirements at each site to keep one policy and avoid local variations
Use the Texas policy as the baseline and ask California employees to waive additional rights
Set global principles and core standards, then add local addenda where law requires more
Let each site manager write attendance rules that fit the local culture and workforce

wrongReasons.A: Extending California standards everywhere breaks the stated funding constraint.
wrongReasons.B: Employees cannot waive California paid sick leave rights, so the waiver approach is unlawful.
wrongReasons.D: Site-by-site rule writing fragments the employee experience and creates uneven compliance.

questions.explanation: Forced distributions on small groups are statistically unreliable and can produce discriminatory selection patterns.
questions.stem: A company adopts forced ranking with the bottom 10% terminated annually, including on teams of six. What is the greatest risk?

choices.text: Lower turnover among top performers, because the ranking system rewards their efforts
A reduced need for documentation, because rankings replace written performance evidence
Higher payroll costs, because terminated employees are replaced at higher salaries
Adverse-impact and discrimination claims from a quota with weak statistical basis in small teams

wrongReasons.A: Lower turnover among top performers is not a risk.
wrongReasons.B: Documentation needs increase, not decrease, when terminations rely on rankings.
wrongReasons.C: Replacement costs are real but secondary to the legal exposure that forced terminations create.

questions.explanation: Jobs are analyzed and valued before pricing, ranges follow pricing, and placement and communication come last.
questions.stem: Arrange these steps of building a job-based pay structure in the best sequence.

items.text: Price benchmark jobs against market survey data
Build pay grades and ranges
Evaluate job worth and rank or group jobs
Conduct job analysis and write job descriptions
Place employees in the structure, communicate it, and administer it

questions.explanation: Managers know why, want it, and know the steps, but cannot yet perform; ability is built through practice and coaching.
questions.stem: After a town hall on a new performance system, 92% of managers say they understand why it is needed and 88% say they support it, and 90% can describe the process steps. Observation shows only 35% complete ratings in the tool correctly. Using ADKAR, which element is the barrier, and what is the best intervention?

choices.text: Reinforcement: recognize the early adopters publicly so others follow their lead
Ability: provide hands-on practice in a sandbox, floor-walking coaches, and protected time
Desire: add incentives for managers who adopt the new system and complete ratings
Awareness: repeat the town hall to reinforce the business case for the new system and its benefits

wrongReasons.A: Reinforcement sustains a change after people can perform; it does not fix inability.
wrongReasons.C: Desire is already high at 88%.
wrongReasons.D: Awareness is already high at 92%.

questions.explanation: Wages, including vested vacation, are due immediately on involuntary termination, and willful delay triggers daily penalties.
questions.stem: A California employer lays off a nonexempt employee on Friday. She has 60 hours of accrued, unused vacation. What does California law require?

choices.text: Pay final wages immediately and pay the accrued vacation hours on the next regular payday
Pay all final wages, including accrued vacation, immediately; late payment triggers waiting-time penalties
Pay final wages by the next regular payday and include the accrued vacation hours in that payment
Pay final wages within 72 hours of the termination date, including the accrued vacation hours

wrongReasons.A: Vested vacation is wages due at the same time as other final pay.
wrongReasons.C: The next-payday rule does not apply to involuntary terminations in California.
wrongReasons.D: The 72-hour rule applies to employees who quit without notice.

questions.explanation: The four Cs describe the dimensions of effective organizational socialization.
questions.stem: Which onboarding framework organizes new-hire activity around compliance, clarification, culture, and connection?

choices.text: The four Cs framework
The four Ps framework
Kirkpatrick's four levels model
The ADDIE design model

wrongReasons.B: The four Ps are a marketing framework.
wrongReasons.C: Kirkpatrick's levels are used to evaluate training.
wrongReasons.D: ADDIE is an instructional design process.

questions.explanation: Employers may express views and opinions without threats, interrogation, promises, or surveillance.
questions.stem: During the campaign, which statement by a supervisor is lawful?

choices.text: Saying the plant may close if the union wins the election and workers lose their jobs
Announcing a new bonus that takes effect the week before the election
Sharing the company's view that a union may reduce flexibility, without threats or promises
Asking employees how they intend to vote in the upcoming union election

wrongReasons.A: Predicting closure as a certain consequence is a threat.
wrongReasons.B: Granting benefits to influence the vote is an unlawful promise or grant.
wrongReasons.D: Polling employees on voting intentions is coercive interrogation.

questions.explanation: Replacing unit employees' work with contractor labor is a mandatory subject of bargaining.
questions.stem: During negotiations, Harbor wants to subcontract delivery work currently done by unit employees. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Harbor may subcontract during negotiations and then bargain about the effects afterward
Subcontracting is bargainable if the union submits a written request within 30 days of the proposal
Subcontracting is a management right that does not require bargaining with the union over its decision
Subcontracting that replaces unit work is generally a mandatory subject, so Harbor must bargain first

wrongReasons.A: Unilateral action before bargaining violates the duty to bargain.
wrongReasons.B: No 30-day written-request rule governs the duty.
wrongReasons.C: No blanket management-rights exception exists absent contract language.

questions.explanation: Economic strikers may be permanently replaced but remain employees with preferential recall rights, while unfair-labor-practice strikers may not be permanently replaced.
questions.stem: The union strikes over wages, which the NLRB would treat as an economic strike. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Harbor may fire the strikers immediately because they are refusing to perform their assigned work
Harbor may permanently replace strikers in both economic and unfair-labor-practice strikes
Harbor must keep the strikers' positions open and may not use replacement workers
Harbor may hire permanent replacements but may not fire strikers; unfair-labor-practice strikes differ

wrongReasons.A: Firing for striking is an unfair labor practice.
wrongReasons.B: Unfair-labor-practice strikers are protected from permanent replacement.
wrongReasons.C: Employers may use temporary and permanent replacements in economic strikes.

questions.explanation: Employers may ask about ability to perform essential functions, and may require post-offer exams if applied to everyone entering the job category.
questions.stem: Which TWO preemployment practices comply with the federal ADA? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Conducting a post-offer medical exam of all entering employees in the same job category
Asking which prescription drugs the candidate takes before an offer
Asking about workers' compensation history before an offer
Requiring a medical exam before any offer is made
Asking whether the candidate can perform the essential functions with or without accommodation

wrongReasons.B: Questions about prescription drugs are disability-related inquiries barred before an offer.
wrongReasons.C: Workers' compensation history inquiries are prohibited before an offer.
wrongReasons.D: Medical exams are barred before a conditional offer.

questions.explanation: A safe harbor plan satisfies nondiscrimination requirements through prescribed employer contributions and notice.
questions.stem: A 401(k) plan repeatedly fails the actual deferral percentage test, forcing refunds to highly compensated employees. Which plan design change eliminates annual testing?

choices.text: Exclude highly compensated employees from the plan so that they do not affect the test
Move plan administration to a new vendor that runs the testing more accurately
Adopt a safe harbor design that provides the required employer contributions and notices
Lower the employer match so that fewer highly compensated employees defer

wrongReasons.A: Excluding highly compensated employees is a harsh design change, not a testing exemption.
wrongReasons.B: A vendor change does not alter the testing requirement.
wrongReasons.D: Cutting the match can worsen test results.

questions.explanation: A significant residual gap needs root-cause review for job-relatedness, followed by targeted, privileged remediation.
questions.stem: A pay analysis of 600 employees shows women earn 9% less than men on average. After a regression controlling for job level, tenure, location, and performance rating, a statistically significant unexplained gap of 2.4% remains. What should HR do first?

choices.text: Report the raw gap to leadership as the headline figure because regression results can be contested by employees
Check whether the remaining drivers, such as starting pay and ratings, are job-related, then plan targeted adjustments
Conclude the gap is explained because the model accounts for most of the difference between the groups
Give women a uniform 2.4% raise immediately to close the measured gap

wrongReasons.A: Suppressing the adjusted result hides the actionable finding.
wrongReasons.C: A significant unexplained gap is a risk signal even when most of the raw gap is explained.
wrongReasons.D: A blanket increase ignores which individuals are actually underpaid and why.

questions.explanation: Scores are 12, 10, 10, and 4, so the key-account loss ranks first under the stated rule.
questions.stem: An HR risk register scores each risk by likelihood (1-5) times impact (1-5), and leadership will fund mitigation in descending order of score. Which risk gets resources first?

choices.text: Loss of a key-account manager: likelihood 4, impact 3
Minor wage-statement error: likelihood 5, impact 2
Office closure from a storm: likelihood 1, impact 4
HRIS data breach: likelihood 2, impact 5

wrongReasons.B: Score is 10, below 12.
wrongReasons.C: Score is 4, the lowest.
wrongReasons.D: Score is 10, below 12.

citations: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.82 (as amended by SB 446, eff. Jan. 1, 2026)
questions.explanation: As amended by SB 446 effective January 1, 2026, California requires notice to affected residents within 30 calendar days of discovering the breach, and a sample notice to the Attorney General within 15 calendar days after notifying residents when more than 500 residents are affected.
questions.stem: A payroll vendor reports a breach exposing the Social Security numbers of 800 California employees. What must the employer do?

choices.text: Wait 90 days for the vendor's forensic report before notifying employees, the state, or regulators
Notify affected employees within 30 calendar days of discovery and send the Attorney General a sample notice within 15 days after that
Notify employees after the vendor confirms that the stolen data were actually misused by criminals
Notify the Federal Trade Commission, which handles breach reports for employers and consumers alike

wrongReasons.A: Delay for a full report conflicts with the 30-calendar-day notice deadline that took effect in 2026.
wrongReasons.C: Notice does not depend on confirmed misuse.
wrongReasons.D: California's duty runs to residents and the state Attorney General, not primarily to the FTC.

questions.explanation: Financial results are lagging indicators; deteriorating engagement and high-performer loss can foreshadow later declines.
questions.stem: Over three years, revenue per employee has risen 12% annually while engagement scores, voluntary turnover among high performers, and time to productivity have all worsened. What is the most defensible interpretation for the executive team?

choices.text: The engagement survey is unreliable because its results contradict the company's financial results
Revenue per employee is the outcome that matters, so the people measures can be deprioritized
Productivity gains may reflect heavier workloads, and the people measures signal future performance risk
High-performer turnover is normal during growth and requires attention if revenue begins to decline

wrongReasons.A: Disagreement between measures is a signal to investigate, not proof of survey error.
wrongReasons.B: Ignoring leading indicators exposes the firm to delayed, larger losses.
wrongReasons.D: Waiting for revenue to fall means acting after the damage appears.

questions.stem: An employee earns $78,000. The pay range for the job runs from $66,000 to $102,000. What is the employee's compa-ratio? Enter it to two decimal places.

questions.explanation: The data point to weak manager connection and role clarity, which structured extended onboarding addresses.
questions.stem: A company loses 45% of new hires within 90 days and finds new hires have little manager contact after the first day. Which redesign is best?

choices.text: Shorten orientation to one day so that new hires reach their teams and start working sooner on real tasks
Lengthen probation periods so that managers can evaluate fit before employees become permanent
Add a sign-on bonus payable after 90 days to keep new hires through the early period
Extend onboarding into a structured 90-day plan with manager check-ins, a buddy, and milestone feedback

wrongReasons.A: A shorter program reduces connection and clarity.
wrongReasons.B: Longer probation does not address the early experience.
wrongReasons.C: A bonus may delay exits without fixing causes.

questions.explanation: FLSA joint employment turns on economic reality; both entities can be liable, and contracts may allocate cost between them but cannot waive statutory liability.
questions.stem: A staffing agency places 25 workers at a manufacturer, which directs their tasks and sets their schedules. A worker claims unpaid overtime under the FLSA. Who may be liable?

choices.text: Both the agency and the manufacturer, as joint employers, based on economic reality
The staffing contract determines liability, so the agency bears it if the contract says so
The manufacturer alone, because it directs the work and sets the schedules
The agency alone, because it hired the workers and runs the payroll

wrongReasons.B: Contract indemnity allocates cost but cannot waive FLSA rights.
wrongReasons.C: The agency's role in hiring and paying can also make it an employer.
wrongReasons.D: Payroll function alone does not determine employer status.
